problems.title: P versus NP
problems.statement: Determine whether P = NP, that is, whether every decision problem whose solutions can be verified in polynomial time by a deterministic Turing machine can also be solved in polynomial time by a deterministic Turing machine.
problems.question: When a yes-or-no problem has short evidence for each yes answer that can be checked in polynomial time, must a deterministic computer also be able to solve the problem in polynomial time? Here polynomial time measures how the work grows with the input size.
problems.why: Equality would give polynomial-time algorithms for every NP decision problem; separation would establish that some efficiently checkable problems resist all such algorithms. This addresses computational efficiency as input size grows.
problems.family: Classical complexity separations
problems.atlasNote: P versus NP remains open on the maintained Clay statement and the bounded claim sweep; no accepted exact-target resolution was established.

consequences.positiveBranch: An equality proof would give deterministic polynomial-time algorithms for every NP decision problem.
consequences.negativeBranch: A separation would establish an NP language with no deterministic polynomial-time decision algorithm.

problems.title: Riemann Hypothesis
problems.statement: For the meromorphic continuation of the Riemann zeta function zeta(s)=sum_{n>=1} n^(-s), initially defined for Re(s)>1, every zero s in the open critical strip 0<Re(s)<1 has Re(s)=1/2. This is the Riemann Hypothesis for zeta alone; it does not assert simplicity of its zeros.
problems.question: Do all zeros of the Riemann zeta function inside the strip with real part between zero and one lie exactly on its middle line?
problems.why: A proof would sharply control fluctuations in the distribution of primes: the prime-counting function would differ from its logarithmic-integral approximation by at most O(√x log x). A disproof would invalidate this equivalent error bound.
problems.family: Riemann hypotheses and exceptional zeros
problems.atlasNote: OpenAI release update, 6 October 2026: the full ranked target remains unclosed by these results. Exact scope reviewed; proofs not independently audited, refereeing not independently confirmed, and Lean artifacts not executed. Family 003: A zero-free half-plane Re(s)>7/8 for zeta excludes only the right-hand part of the critical strip. The target requires every nontrivial zero to have real part exactly 1/2; no conclusion excluding zeros between 1/2 and 7/8 is supplied. This is partial zero-location progress, not the Riemann Hypothesis. Earlier qualification retained: Riemann remains open. September 2026 progress on the proportion of simple critical-line zeros is partial, not proof that every nontrivial zero lies on the line. Uncorroborated or inaccessible proof claims were not accepted.

consequences.positiveBranch: A proof establishes the equivalent pi(x)=Li(x)+O(sqrt(x)log(x)) bound described by Bombieri, sharply controlling prime-counting fluctuations. Applications requiring additional L-function hypotheses are not automatically obtained.
consequences.negativeBranch: A disproof makes that equivalent prime-counting error bound false and supplies an obstruction to the proposed zeta-zero pattern. Other conditional implications remain valid as implications; their conclusions do not automatically all fail.

problems.title: Yang-Mills Existence and Mass Gap
problems.statement: For every compact simple gauge group G, prove that a nontrivial four-dimensional quantum Yang-Mills theory on R^4 exists with all existence requirements of Jaffe-Witten, Quantum Yang-Mills Theory, sections 3-4, including axiomatic properties at least as strong as their cited references [45,35], the required gauge-invariant local fields and short-distance compatibility specified there. Its vacuum Hamiltonian H has no spectrum in (0,Delta) for some Delta > 0, and the supremum of such Delta is finite. The official reconstruction and existence requirements are retained by reference, not replaced by an unrestricted equivalence of arbitrary Euclidean and Minkowski theories. An isolated first excited eigenstate, confinement and asymptotic completeness are not additional requirements.
problems.question: Can a nontrivial Yang–Mills quantum field theory in four-dimensional spacetime be constructed rigorously for every compact simple gauge group—the choice of internal symmetry—with a positive, finite gap between vacuum energy and the remaining energy spectrum?
problems.why: The construction would turn the specified four-dimensional quantum gauge-field model into a theory satisfying the required mathematical axioms. Its spectrum would have a positive, finite gap above vacuum energy, without requiring an isolated first excited eigenstate.
problems.family: Yang-Mills Existence and Mass Gap
problems.atlasNote: The universal four-dimensional Yang–Mills existence/mass-gap target remains open. Three-dimensional outlines, individual gauge-group claims and withdrawn postings do not establish the full target.

consequences.positiveBranch: A positive resolution rigorously constructs the official theory and establishes positive finite spectral mass for all permitted groups; it does not automatically prove confinement or every proposed extension.
consequences.negativeBranch: A negative resolution identifies a permitted group for which the official conjunction cannot hold, forcing revision of that universal mathematical target without by itself invalidating experimental observations or every other quantum field theory.

problems.title: Hodge Conjecture
problems.statement: Determine whether every rational Hodge class on a smooth complex projective algebraic variety is a rational linear combination of classes of algebraic subvarieties (algebraic cycles).
problems.question: Hodge theory singles out certain rational cohomology classes, which encode topological features of a smooth complex projective variety. Must every such class be a rational combination of classes represented by algebraic subvarieties?
problems.why: Cohomology records features of a variety, while algebraic cycles are built from its algebraic subvarieties. A proof would show that every rational class of the specified Hodge type can be accounted for by those algebraic pieces.
problems.family: Hodge conjectures
problems.atlasNote: OpenAI release update, 6 October 2026: the full ranked target remains unclosed by these results. Exact scope reviewed; proofs not independently audited, refereeing not independently confirmed, and Lean artifacts not executed. Family 032: The target quantifies over every smooth complex projective variety and every rational Hodge class. The family proves that assertion for CM abelian varieties, arbitrary products of projective K3 surfaces, and the specified additional abelian/cover families, in the stated codimensions. These are substantial subclasses, not all smooth projective varieties; none of the abstracts gives a reduction of the universal target to them. Earlier qualification retained: The rational Hodge conjecture remains open. Conditional witness axioms, selected Fermat varieties and inaccessible full-proof claims do not establish the all-varieties target.

consequences.positiveBranch: A proof would express every rational Hodge class on every smooth complex projective variety as a rational combination of algebraic-cycle classes.
consequences.negativeBranch: A counterexample would be a rational Hodge class outside the span of algebraic-cycle classes.

problems.title: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture
problems.statement: Prove or disprove that, for every elliptic curve E over the rational numbers, the rank of the finitely generated abelian group E(Q) of rational points equals the order of vanishing at s = 1 of the associated Hasse–Weil L-function L(E, s).
problems.question: For an elliptic curve over the rational numbers, its rank counts the independent infinite-order generators of its group of rational points. Does this rank equal the order of vanishing of its L-function at s = 1—the multiplicity of the zero there, taken as zero when the function is nonzero?
problems.why: A proof would identify an algebraic measure of the curve’s rational points with an analytic measurement of its L-function. A counterexample would locate a curve where those two measurements differ.
problems.family: Elliptic curve ranks and congruent numbers
problems.atlasNote: OpenAI release update, 6 October 2026: the full ranked target remains unclosed by these results. Exact scope reviewed; proofs not independently audited, refereeing not independently confirmed, and Lean artifacts not executed. Family 002: The target is equality of analytic and Mordell-Weil ranks for every E/Q, rather than the full leading-term formula. This family gives that equality and the stronger leading-term conclusion when the full q-power Selmer corank is zero or one for some prime q. It leaves curves outside that hypothesis untreated, so it is a low-corank subcase only. Family 004: The companion proves rank equality for E/Q with nonzero rational two-torsion and full 2-power Selmer corank zero or one, allowing arbitrary reduction at 2. The BSD rank target includes every E/Q without either restriction, so this is a limited subcase and does not follow as a full closure from the H10 result. Family 006: The low-corank 2-converse explicitly gives equality of analytic and Mordell-Weil ranks for E/Q whose full 2-power Selmer corank is zero or one. The family also supplies analytic rank densities and their mean over twists, but an average or density-one assertion does not prove rank equality for every curve or every twist. Earlier qualification retained: BSD rank equality remains open. The located all-rank working-draft claim lacks independent acceptance; recent uses and special cases do not supply a universal proof.

consequences.positiveBranch: A proof would equate Mordell-Weil rank with analytic rank for every elliptic curve over the rational numbers.
consequences.negativeBranch: A counterexample would be an elliptic curve whose rational-point rank differs from the order of vanishing of its L-function at one.

problems.title: Navier-Stokes Existence and Smoothness: Fefferman A
problems.statement: Prove Fefferman statement (A): for every viscosity nu > 0 and every real smooth divergence-free Schwartz vector field u0 on R^3, with force f identically zero, there are real velocity u and pressure p in C-infinity(R^3 x [0,infinity)) satisfying partial_t u + (u dot grad)u = nu Delta u - grad p, div u = 0 and u(x,0) = u0(x). The velocity energy integral over R^3 of |u(x,t)|^2 is bounded above by one finite constant for all t >= 0; that constant may depend on u0 and nu. Schwartz means every spatial derivative decays faster than every inverse polynomial, as in official condition (4). Smoothness includes time zero. The selected domain is whole space, not the torus.
problems.question: For an incompressible fluid filling three-dimensional space, with any positive viscosity and no external force, does every smooth, rapidly decaying initial velocity give a flow that stays smooth forever, with uniformly bounded total kinetic energy?
problems.why: This asks whether the specified three-dimensional viscous-flow equations can evolve every allowed starting flow for unlimited time without developing a singularity, while keeping total kinetic energy bounded.
problems.family: Incompressible fluid regularity
problems.atlasNote: The ranked target is Fefferman A: unforced whole-space Navier–Stokes regularity for smooth rapidly decaying divergence-free data. OpenAI's September claim addresses forced alternatives C/D, not A. Retain open for this exact target; no proof acceptance is inferred from the broader prize announcement.

consequences.positiveBranch: A positive resolution guarantees global smooth unforced evolution with the selected energy bound for every allowed datum; it does not automatically establish every broader data or forcing formulation.
consequences.negativeBranch: A negative resolution proves failure of that precise global existence claim for a permitted viscosity and datum under zero force. It does not itself settle the periodic alternative or unrelated forced problems.

problems.title: Global Langlands Functoriality Conjecture
problems.statement: For every number field F, quasisplit connected reductive F-groups G-prime and G, and admissible L-homomorphism rho:L(G-prime)->L(G) (over Gamma_F, commuting with its projections, in Arthur Principle1.1's convention), every automorphic representation pi-prime of G-prime(A_F), in the inclusive Langlands sense cited there, has an automorphic representation pi of G(A_F) whose unramified Satake classes equal the images under rho_v of those of pi-prime outside a finite set of places. This is existence of a weak transfer, not uniqueness or a prescribed transfer function.
problems.question: Langlands L-groups encode symmetries used to organize automorphic representations. For quasisplit reductive groups over number fields, does every admissible map between their L-groups transfer these representations while matching their local arithmetic data at all but finitely many places?
problems.why: A proof would guarantee the stated transfer across every group map in scope, linking automorphic representations through their local parameters. The existence claim permits more than one transfer and leaves its exceptional places finite.
problems.family: Langlands functoriality and modularity
problems.atlasNote: Retain open_with_solved_subcases for the frozen global functoriality target. Existing restricted transfers and recent conjectural use do not establish the full specified transfer theorem; current universal status evidence remains bounded.

consequences.positiveBranch: Prove weak automorphic transfer for every specified F, group pair, L-homomorphism and inclusive automorphic representation.
consequences.negativeBranch: Prove existence of one such F, group pair, L-homomorphism and automorphic representation with no automorphic weak transfer; no explicit example is required.

problems.title: Existence of One-Way Functions
problems.statement: Prove or disprove that there exists a deterministic polynomial-time computable function family f_n:{0,1}^n->{0,1}^{poly(n)} such that every probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm inverts f_n on a uniformly random input with only negligible probability.
problems.question: Do one-way functions exist: functions that a deterministic computer can evaluate in polynomial time, but that every randomized polynomial-time algorithm reverses on a random input’s output with success eventually smaller than every inverse power of the input length? Reversing means finding any input with that output.
problems.why: A construction would unconditionally separate efficient forward computation from hard inversion on random inputs, even when the inverter uses randomness. Every randomized polynomial-time inverter would have only negligible success probability as input length grows.
problems.family: One-way functions and permutations
problems.atlasNote: Normalize to open: unconditional existence of the frozen one-way functions has not been proved. Conditional constructions and hardness characterizations do not constitute an unconditional solved subcase of this existential target. This is status-label cleanup, not a newly discovered mathematical reversal.

consequences.positiveBranch: An unconditional construction with a proof of negligible PPT inversion probability would establish existence under the standard definition and instantiate consequences already proved from OWFs.
consequences.negativeBranch: An impossibility theorem for every polynomial-time function family under the standard inversion experiment would rule out classical one-way functions and assumptions equivalent to their existence.

problems.title: The abc Conjecture of Masser and Oesterle
problems.statement: Prove that for every epsilon > 0, there exists a constant C(epsilon) such that for all coprime positive integers a + b = c, c < C(epsilon) rad(abc)^{1+epsilon}.
problems.question: Suppose coprime positive integers satisfy a + b = c, and R is the product of the distinct primes dividing abc. For every positive ε, is c less than C(ε) times R^(1 + ε), with one constant C(ε) working for every such triple?
problems.why: A proof would uniformly restrict how large an additive triple can be relative to its distinct prime factors. A disproof would find a positive epsilon for which no constant controls all such triples.
problems.family: abc and Szpiro conjectures
problems.atlasNote: abc retains open_disputed_claim. Joshi's February 2025 revision is not adjudicated by the older Scholze–Stix objection to Mochizuki; the July 2026 abc-type proposal is another conjecture. Current acceptance of a full proof was not established.

consequences.positiveBranch: A proof would establish the stated radical bound uniformly for every epsilon and all coprime positive integer triples a + b = c.
consequences.negativeBranch: A disproof would exhibit some positive epsilon for which no constant gives the stated radical bound over all coprime triples.

problems.title: Extended Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions
problems.statement: For every algebraic number field K (a finite extension of Q, including K=Q), does every zero s of its Dedekind zeta function ζ_K(s) in the critical strip 0<Re(s)<1 satisfy Re(s)=1/2?
problems.question: Every number field—a finite algebraic extension of the rationals—has a Dedekind zeta function. Must all its zeros with real part between zero and one lie on the middle line, with real part one-half?
problems.why: A proof would supply the zeta-function hypothesis used in effective Chebotarev estimates for how primes split in number fields, with their other conditions retained. Including the rational field would also establish the ordinary Riemann Hypothesis.
problems.family: Riemann hypotheses and exceptional zeros
problems.atlasNote: OpenAI release update, 6 October 2026: the full ranked target remains unclosed by these results. Exact scope reviewed; proofs not independently audited, refereeing not independently confirmed, and Lean artifacts not executed. Family 003: The stated half-plane theorem applies to zeta_Q and, by the usual abelian L-function factorization, to Dedekind zeta functions in the abelian settings represented by its Dirichlet/finite-order Hecke factors. It supplies neither the critical line 1/2 nor all number fields, so it is only restricted zero-free progress for the universal Dedekind-zeta target. Earlier qualification retained: Retain open_disputed_claim for Dedekind ERH. Zhang's posting was revised to v19 on September 14, 2026; objections or prior assessments of v18 must not be represented as reviews of v19. No independent acceptance of the newest claim was established.

consequences.positiveBranch: A proof would establish the all-fields zero-location assertion and supply the Dedekind-GRH hypothesis used in effective Chebotarev estimates, retaining those estimates' stated degree, discriminant and range conditions. It would also settle ordinary RH through K=Q.
consequences.negativeBranch: A disproof would exhibit or prove the existence of a failure of the all-fields assertion. A failure at K=Q refutes ordinary RH; a failure only at another field need not. It would invalidate using universal ERH as an established premise, but need not refute every conditional consequence separately.

problems.title: NP versus P/poly
problems.statement: Determine the truth of NP subseteq P/poly. Here NP consists of languages over finite binary strings accepted by nondeterministic Turing machines in polynomial time. P/poly consists of languages L for which there exist constants C>=1 and integer k>=1 and Boolean circuits C_n for all n>=0, of size at most C(n+1)^k, deciding membership in L on every length-n input. Circuits are finite acyclic single-output circuits with fan-in-two AND/OR, fan-in-one NOT, input bits and hardwired constants0/1; count all nodes. Each language has its own bound and circuit family, with no uniform generation requirement.
problems.question: Can every yes-or-no problem with short, efficiently checkable evidence for yes answers be solved by Boolean circuits of polynomial size, if a separate circuit may be chosen for each input length? No efficient method of constructing those circuits is required.
problems.why: Containment would collapse the polynomial hierarchy to its second level by the Karp–Lipton theorem. Noncontainment would establish a general circuit-size barrier for an NP language and imply P ≠ NP.
problems.family: NP versus P/poly
problems.atlasNote: NP containment in nonuniform P/poly remains open; February 2026 notes pose the matching general-circuit question. Restricted circuits and Karp–Lipton implications do not decide it.

consequences.positiveBranch: By the Karp–Lipton theorem, NP containment in P/poly collapses the polynomial hierarchy to its second level. The circuits' nonuniform existence alone does not give a deterministic polynomial-time SAT algorithm.
consequences.negativeBranch: Noncontainment gives a superpolynomial general Boolean-circuit obstruction for an NP language and implies P!=NP because P is contained in P/poly. It does not by itself establish average-case hardness or secure cryptography.

problems.title: Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions
problems.statement: For every integer q>=1 and every Dirichlet character chi modulo q, including principal and imprimitive characters, every zero s of the meromorphic continuation of L(s,chi)=sum_{n>=1}chi(n)n^(-s) in 0<Re(s)<1 satisfies Re(s)=1/2. The continuation is from Re(s)>1. Only open-strip zeros are quantified: principal-character poles and boundary zeros of imprimitive Euler factors are not counterexamples. No simplicity or central nonvanishing requirement is added.
problems.question: Dirichlet L-functions extend the zeta-function setting by using periodic arithmetic weights. For every Dirichlet character, do all zeros of its L-function with real part between zero and one lie on the middle line, with real part one-half?
problems.why: A proof would bound how far one must search for a prime in an arithmetic progression. For q > 3 and a coprime to q, the least prime congruent to a modulo q would be at most (φ(q) log q)², where φ(q) counts the residue classes coprime to q.
problems.family: Riemann hypotheses and exceptional zeros
problems.atlasNote: OpenAI release update, 6 October 2026: the full ranked target remains unclosed by these results. Exact scope reviewed; proofs not independently audited, refereeing not independently confirmed, and Lean artifacts not executed. Family 003: The theorem includes every Dirichlet L-function and allows the principal pole, but its zero-free boundary is 7/8 rather than 1/2. Thus its character quantification agrees broadly with the target while its zero-location conclusion is strictly weaker. The GRH target remains unresolved. Earlier qualification retained: Dirichlet GRH remains open. No independently established full-target resolution was obtained; neighboring Riemann-family claims and source-access limitations remain qualified.

consequences.positiveBranch: A proof makes LLS's GRH-conditional least-prime estimate unconditional: for q>3 and gcd(a,q)=1, the least prime congruent to a modulo q is at most (phi(q)log(q))^2.
consequences.negativeBranch: A disproof establishes an off-line Dirichlet zero and invalidates the general hypothesis. Theorems conditional on GRH remain true implications; particular prime-distribution or algorithmic conclusions are not thereby automatically false.

problems.title: NP versus coNP Problem
problems.statement: Determine whether NP = coNP, that is, whether the class NP is closed under complementation. Equivalently, by the Cook-Reckhow criterion, decide whether there exists a polynomially bounded propositional proof system.
problems.question: Whenever yes answers to a decision problem have polynomial-length certificates checkable in polynomial time, do its no answers always have such certificates as well?
problems.why: Equality would make NP closed under exchanging yes and no answers and provide a polynomially bounded propositional proof system. Separation would rule out every such proof system.
problems.family: Classical complexity separations
problems.atlasNote: NP versus coNP remains open with an explicit claim warning. Lin's August 2026 v28 and Gordeev–Haeusler's May 2026 revision make opposing claims; older independent critiques do not automatically adjudicate those revisions. Restricted proof-system lower bounds are not the full separation.

consequences.positiveBranch: An equality proof would show that NP is closed under complement and yield a polynomially bounded propositional proof system.
consequences.negativeBranch: A separation would give an NP language whose complement is not in NP and rule out every polynomially bounded propositional proof system.

problems.title: P versus PSPACE
problems.statement: Determine whether P = PSPACE, that is, whether every language decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial space is decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time.
problems.question: Can every yes-or-no problem solvable by a deterministic computer using polynomially bounded memory also be solved deterministically in time polynomial in the input length?
problems.why: Equality would turn every polynomial-space decision procedure into a polynomial-time one. Separation would establish that some problems admit modest memory requirements while resisting every deterministic polynomial-time algorithm.
problems.family: Classical complexity separations
problems.atlasNote: P versus PSPACE remains open. Recent space simulations and fixed-exponent time lower bounds do not separate polynomial time from polynomial space; conditional equality implications are not unconditional resolutions.

consequences.positiveBranch: An equality proof would convert every polynomial-space decision procedure into a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm.
consequences.negativeBranch: A separation would exhibit a language in PSPACE that is not in P.

problems.title: Tate Conjecture for Algebraic Cycles
problems.statement: For every smooth geometrically irreducible projective variety X over a field k finitely generated over its prime field, every codimension i, and every prime l different from char(k), prove that the l-adic cycle-class map from codimension-i algebraic cycle classes defined over k, tensored with Q_l, is surjective onto H^(2i)(X_bar,Q_l(i))^Gal(k_bar/k).
problems.question: Algebraic subvarieties defined over the base field produce l-adic cohomology classes fixed by arithmetic symmetries after a normalization called a Tate twist. For smooth projective varieties over finitely generated fields, are all even-degree classes with this symmetry property generated by algebraic cycles over the same field, for every prime l different from the field’s characteristic?
problems.why: A proof would recover every invariant class in the specified cohomology from algebraic cycles defined over the base field. A counterexample would identify an invariant class with no such algebraic description.
problems.family: Tate Conjecture for Algebraic Cycles
problems.atlasNote: OpenAI release update, 6 October 2026: the full ranked target remains unclosed by these results. Exact scope reviewed; proofs not independently audited, refereeing not independently confirmed, and Lean artifacts not executed. Family 001: The supplied paper establishes a precise algebraicity result for specializations of rational Hodge classes on good-reduction abelian varieties, not surjectivity for all Tate classes. Its setup fixes an algebraic closure of Q inside C and a p-adic place, takes the reduction over the algebraic closure of F_p, and defines good reduction after descent to a number field and finite extension at that place. Thus the resulting rational algebraic cycle is on the geometric special fiber; the source does not directly require it to be defined over any preselected finitely generated base k. The additional algebraicity consequence uses the CM Hodge theorem and is distinct from Theorem 1.1, which is only the rational pairing statement. A precise finite-field consequence is available for a specialized class that is invariant over a chosen finite field of definition: the cycle descends to a finite extension, and its normalized trace gives a rational cycle over the chosen field with that invariant l-adic class. This ordinary descent implication does not show that every invariant class is a specialization of the stated kind. No general Tate resolution, or resolution for all classes on every abelian variety, follows from the supplied statements. Family 032: The catalogue explicitly derives the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields. The ranked target additionally quantifies over arbitrary smooth projective varieties over every field finitely generated over its prime field. Neither nonabelian varieties nor the general finitely generated base-field scope is supplied by this consequence, so the universal rational cycle-class surjectivity target remains open in this mapping. Earlier qualification retained: Retain the rational Tate conjecture as open_with_solved_subcases. Integral counterexamples do not refute the frozen rational cycle map. Kahn's unsuccessful surface approach does not prove the universal target; its HTML/history date discrepancy is not treated as an authenticated new revision.

consequences.positiveBranch: A proof would identify every invariant l-adic cohomology class of even degree with a cycle class defined over the base field in the stated generality.
consequences.negativeBranch: A counterexample would exhibit a Galois-invariant l-adic class outside the span of algebraic cycle classes and disprove the general conjecture.

problems.title: BQP Versus NP: Complete Language-Class Relation
problems.statement: Determine the truth values of BOTH NP subseteq BQP and BQP subseteq NP for unrelativized, advice-free classes of total languages over {0,1}. NP consists of languages with polynomial-length binary witnesses and a deterministic polynomial-time verifier. BQP consists of languages decided by polynomial-time uniformly generated polynomial-size quantum circuits (a deterministic Turing machine outputs Q_n on 1^n), using Watrous's fixed Toffoli, Hadamard and phase-i gates with |0> ancillas and discarding, followed by a standard-basis output measurement. On every yes input acceptance is at least 2/3, and on every no input it is at most 1/3. No arbitrary real gate constants, advice or oracle are available. Establish equality, either proper containment, or incomparability.
problems.question: How do efficient quantum solving and efficient classical verification compare for yes-or-no problems? Does quantum computation with bounded error solve every problem with short, efficiently checkable evidence for yes answers—and do all problems it solves have such evidence?
problems.why: Resolving both inclusions would determine whether these computational classes coincide, one strictly contains the other, or neither contains the other. Each outcome gives a different relationship between efficient verification and bounded-error quantum computation.
problems.family: BQP Versus NP: Complete Language-Class Relation
problems.atlasNote: Both unrelativized BQP/NP inclusions remain unresolved on the checked evidence. Random-permutation oracle separations do not settle the frozen uniform total-language relationship.

consequences.completeResolution: A full determination fixes whether efficient quantum computation encompasses all NP languages and whether every BQP language admits efficient classical witness verification. problems.title: Matrix-Multiplication Exponent Equals Two
problems.statement: Let R_Q(n) be the tensor rank over Q of the bilinear map multiplying two n by n rational matrices: the least r for which AB is a sum of r products alpha_j(A) beta_j(B) C_j, with rational linear forms alpha_j, beta_j and rational output matrices C_j. Set omega_Q = inf{tau in R : R_Q(n) = O(n^tau)}. Prove omega_Q = 2. Equivalently, for every epsilon > 0, exact multiplication admits division-free arithmetic circuits over Q of size O(n^(2+epsilon)), counting rational additions, subtractions, multiplications and constant scalar operations at unit cost. Circuits need not be uniformly generated and rational coefficient bit lengths are not charged. Constants and thresholds may depend on epsilon. Literal O(n^2) attainment is not required.
problems.question: Can two n-by-n rational matrices be multiplied exactly, without division, with a number of arithmetic operations arbitrarily close to quadratic: O(n^(2 + ε)) for every positive ε? Each rational arithmetic operation counts as one step, regardless of the number of bits in its operands.
problems.why: A proof would allow exact matrix multiplication with arithmetic exponents arbitrarily close to two and carry through applicable algebraic reductions to other computations. The statement measures arithmetic operations; it leaves coefficient bit costs and literal quadratic attainment outside its guarantee.

problems.title: Prove the Penrose inequality or present a counterexample
problems.statement: Let (M,g,k) be a three-dimensional asymptotically flat initial data set for the Einstein equations satisfying the dominant energy condition and containing an outermost apparent horizon. If A is the least area needed to enclose that horizon and m_ADM is the ADM mass, prove the sharp spacetime Penrose inequality m_ADM >= sqrt(A/(16*pi)), with the appropriate Schwarzschild rigidity statement, or construct initial data satisfying the hypotheses that violate the inequality.
problems.question: For isolated gravitational initial data in three spatial dimensions obeying the dominant energy condition, must an outermost apparent horizon force the total mass to satisfy m ≥ √(A/(16π)), where A is the least area enclosing it, with equality characterized by Schwarzschild geometry?
problems.why: A proof would give a sharp lower bound on total mass from the least area enclosing the horizon and identify the equality geometry. A counterexample would show that the stated geometric and energy conditions permit a mass below the proposed area-based bound.
problems.family: Prove the Penrose inequality or present a counterexample
problems.atlasNote: OpenAI release update, 6 October 2026: the full ranked target remains unclosed by these results. Exact scope reviewed; proofs not independently audited, refereeing not independently confirmed, and Lean artifacts not executed. Family 260: The numerical three-dimensional enclosing-area inequality is stated with ordinary differentiated asymptotic flatness g-delta=O2(r^-q), K=O1(r^(-1-q)), q>1/2, integrable constraint densities, finite ADM limits, completeness, dominant energy, and weakly future trapped boundary. Theorem 1.5 derives positivity of the enclosing area and strict ADM timelikeness, so these are not leftover assumptions for that class. The enclosing cuts count the whole boundary, including coincident and disconnected pieces, matching least enclosing area. Setting n=3 in the stated coefficient gives sqrt(A/(16*pi)); invariant ADM mass also implies the same lower bound for ADM energy if the frozen m_ADM uses that convention. Arbitrary second fundamental form and momentum are allowed, and the newer introduction reports a finitely-many-end formulation with specified cut conventions. The unresolved part of full literal coverage is rigidity: the supplied original-data theorem imposes a connected, outer area-minimizing, outermost horizon class and stronger differentiated decay; the newer stated equality result permits multiple initial components but still requires outer area minimization and a specified strong outermostness condition. These extra requirements are not consequences of merely saying outermost apparent horizon in the frozen dossier. The numerical theorem is therefore covered in the stated AF class, with substantial original-data rigidity, but the complete frozen inequality-plus-rigidity target cannot yet be marked fully covered without fixing its equality and designated-end conventions. Earlier qualification retained: The sharp spacetime Penrose inequality remains open_with_solved_subcases. Located MOTS and geometric extensions retain extra hypotheses or a weaker constant; no full sharp unconditional proof was verified.

consequences.positiveBranch: A general proof with the sharp constant would extend the established Riemannian and conditional spacetime cases and characterize equality by Schwarzschild initial data under the final hypotheses.
consequences.negativeBranch: A counterexample would delimit the geometric or energy hypotheses under which horizon area can control ADM mass and require a revised spacetime inequality.

problems.title: Modularity of Elliptic Curves over Number Fields (End_K(E)=Z)
problems.statement: For every number field K and every elliptic curve E/K with End_K(E)=Z, prove that pi(E) admits a GL_2(A_K^infinity)-equivariant injection into A tensor_Q C, exactly as in Thorne's Conjecture 2.6. Here A is the direct limit over open compact U of H^*(Y_U,Q) for the adelic locally symmetric spaces defined on page 647, and pi(E) is the restricted tensor product at all finite places v of rec_{K_v}^{-1}(r_v tensor |.|^{1/2},N_v), with (r_v,N_v) attached to E in the source's geometric-Frobenius normalization on pages 646 and 649.
problems.question: For any number field K, does every elliptic curve whose K-defined endomorphisms are just integer multiplications have the predicted automorphic realization: an embedding of its finite-place representation into the cohomology of the associated arithmetic spaces?
problems.why: A proof would realize the arithmetic data encoded by the curve’s specified finite-place representation inside the cohomology of those spaces. The injection would respect the adelic group action, connecting the curve’s local representations with this geometric construction.

problems.atlasNote: OpenAI release update, 6 October 2026: the full ranked target remains unclosed by these results. Exact scope reviewed; proofs not independently audited, refereeing not independently confirmed, and Lean artifacts not executed. Family 030: Theorem 1.1 covers every elliptic curve over every imaginary quadratic field and matches all finite local parameters, not just good-reduction L-factors. It quantifies over every auxiliary l and coefficient embedding, allowing l different from each specified finite place v. Section 2 explicitly uses geometric Frobenius and rec( pi_v tensor |det|^(-1/2) ) for the cohomological realization. Moving this twist to the Weil parameter gives precisely the target rec^-1(r_v tensor |.|^(1/2),N_v). Weight zero is explicitly the algebraic weight of trivial coefficients, the required cohomological normalization. For End_K(E)=Z, the non-CM case is cuspidal, and geometrically CM curves with CM not defined over K retain the induced cuspidal case; the split isobaric branch when the CM field is already K is not substituted for eligible curves. The usual cuspidal cohomological realization therefore supplies the expected imaginary-quadratic subcase of the injection target, with the cohomology step identified as an existing standard implication rather than a theorem quoted verbatim from this extract. Neither the field quantifier nor the exact local normalization is weakened. The universal target over all number fields remains unresolved. Earlier qualification retained: Modularity over arbitrary number fields remains open_with_solved_subcases for the frozen End_K(E)=Z scope. Totally real tower and odd-degree uniformization results are restricted or conditional; End_K(E)=Z is not silently replaced by geometrically non-CM.

consequences.positiveBranch: The specified geometric representations would occur in the cohomology for every eligible elliptic curve over every number field; the source deduces cuspidal automorphic representations and matching L-functions, giving their analytic continuation. A full BSD theorem, effective algorithms, or all automorphic functoriality do not follow automatically.
consequences.negativeBranch: A proof that no required injection exists for one eligible curve would refute this precise universal geometric-automorphy assertion and identify a boundary of that expectation. problems.title: BQP versus QMA
problems.statement: For promise problems A=(A_yes,A_no) with disjoint sets of finite binary strings, use polynomial-time uniform quantum circuits over a fixed effectively specified finite universal gate set, with polynomially many gates and |0> ancillas and a measured output bit. BQP has such a circuit accepting each yes input with probability>=2/3 and each no input with probability<=1/3. QMA permits a polynomial-length quantum witness: each yes input has a witness accepted with probability>=2/3, and every witness on each no input is accepted with probability<=1/3. Outside the promise no condition is imposed. Is QMA contained in BQP, equivalently BQP=QMA?
problems.question: If a quantum computer can efficiently check a supplied quantum proof for a promised yes-or-no problem, can it also solve that problem efficiently without receiving the proof? Both verification and solving allow bounded error.
problems.why: Equality would give efficient quantum decision procedures for QMA-complete promise problems, including the standard local-Hamiltonian energy-threshold problem. Separation would show that quantum witnesses add decision power beyond efficient quantum computation alone.
problems.family: BQP versus QMA
problems.atlasNote: BQP versus QMA remains open for unrelativized uniform promise classes. Unitary/classical oracle results and August qIO work with an assumed average-case QMA gap do not decide that equality.

consequences.positiveBranch: Equality would yield efficient bounded-error quantum decision procedures for QMA-complete promise problems, including the standard two-local Hamiltonian energy-threshold problem. It would not automatically prepare witnesses or ground states or break every quantum cryptographic primitive.
consequences.negativeBranch: Separation would prove that quantum verification with polynomial quantum proofs is strictly stronger than witness-free efficient quantum decision computation. QMA-completeness would then rule out BQP decision algorithms for the standard complete promise problems.

problems.title: The Fontaine-Mazur Conjecture on Geometric Galois Representations
problems.statement: Let K be a number field and l a prime. Every irreducible continuous finite-dimensional l-adic representation rho of Gal(Kbar/K), unramified outside finitely many places and de Rham at every place above l, occurs as a subquotient of H^i_et(X_Kbar)(m) for some smooth projective variety X over K, integer i >= 0, and integer Tate twist m. Etale cohomology is taken with the same l-adic coefficient field as rho. There is no nonnegative Hodge-Tate weight restriction.
problems.question: A Galois representation records arithmetic symmetries as matrices. Must every irreducible l-adic representation over a number field, unramified outside finitely many places and de Rham at primes above l—a local condition describing behavior expected from geometry—come from a smooth projective variety’s cohomology, allowing subquotients and Tate twists?
problems.why: A proof would make these arithmetic conditions sufficient for geometric realization across all number fields and finite dimensions. The realization may use any integer Tate twist, including negative twists, and imposes no nonnegative Hodge–Tate weight restriction.
problems.family: The Fontaine-Mazur Conjecture on Geometric Galois Representations
problems.atlasNote: OpenAI release update, 6 October 2026: the full ranked target remains unclosed by these results. Exact scope reviewed; proofs not independently audited, refereeing not independently confirmed, and Lean artifacts not executed. Family 010: The classical-modularity companion treats odd, regular, irreducible two-dimensional representations of G_Q at l=2, de Rham at 2 and finitely ramified. Modular forms supply geometric realizations in that setting, but Fontaine-Mazur quantifies over all number fields, dimensions and primes without oddness or distinct-weight restrictions. The separate completed-Hecke pro-modularity result explicitly does not assert classical modularity and must not be used to remove the de Rham condition. Earlier qualification retained: The full corrected assertion is open_with_solved_subcases as a scope-based current-status inference, not proof certification. Newton describes dimension-one cases and Thorne August2026 states a narrower still-conjectural GL2 case with restricted new results. No claim of universal present-status quotation is made.

consequences.positiveBranch: The arithmetic hypotheses would suffice for twisted geometric realization throughout the frozen scope. This is the direct meaning of the assertion in Hajir and Shin–Templier, not an algorithm for finding a variety. Newton's additional automorphy and L-function consequences explicitly require Langlands reciprocity.
consequences.negativeBranch: A qualifying representation with no such realization would refute sufficiency of the stated hypotheses, while preserving already proved cases. This is the logical complement of the sourced geometric-realization assertion; it would not by itself refute theorems about cohomology or prove a failure of Langlands reciprocity.

problems.title: Equivariant Tamagawa number conjecture: Burns-Flach Conjecture4 package
problems.statement: For every motive M over a number field K in Burns-Flach Section3.1's motivic-structure formalism, with an action of a finite-dimensional semisimple Q-algebra A, and every order mathcal A in A admitting the compatible projective mathcal A-structure of Section3.3, prove Burns-Flach Conjecture4(i)-(iv) in its stated conditional setting. The external defining hypotheses are the finite motivic cohomology and real comparison exact sequence of Conjecture1, the motivic-to-p-adic comparison of Conjecture2 for M and Mdual(1), coefficient compatibility giving well-defined equivariant local factors as in4.1 (Conjecture3 or the weaker Euler-factor compatibility of Remark7), and the stated Coherence hypothesis. A projective structure consists of full projective lattices in the archimedean realizations whose l-adic comparison images agree and are Galois-stable, not merely an arbitrary maximal-order choice. The INCLUDED assertions are: (i) the finite equivariant L-function L(AM,s) has meromorphic continuation to0; (ii) its componentwise integer order r equals rr_A(H_f^1(K,Mdual(1))^*)-rr_A(H_f^0(K,Mdual(1))^*), with reduced rank as in2.6; (iii) for the nonzero componentwise leading Laurent coefficient L*(AM,0)=lim_(s->0) s^(-r)L(AM,s), the class T_Omega=delta_hat^1_(mathcal A,R)(L*(AM,0))+R_Omega(M,mathcal A) lies in Cl(mathcal A,Q); and (iv) T_Omega=0 in Cl(mathcal A,R), hence in K_0(mathcal A,R). The R_Omega term is the class of the fundamental virtual object with its integral compact-support cohomology structures and real comparison trivialization in3.4; delta_hat is Lemma9's canonical extended reduced-norm boundary, not an inverse to a surjective real reduced norm. Equivalently the final identity is delta_hat(L*)=-R_Omega. Preserve graded determinant conventions and all suitable nonmaximal/noncommutative orders. Coherence-free Remark8's Conjecture5 and Conjecture6 for EVERY prime are an alternative to the rational/integral clauses in the source's stated sense, not removal of(i)-(ii) or replacement by a single p-local or epsilon assertion. The external hypotheses are not presumed universally proved or restricted to currently established cases, and proving all of them is not added as a separate conclusion.
problems.question: For a motive over a number field with extra symmetries, possibly noncommuting, does its equivariant L-function continue to s = 0, allowing poles, with the predicted zero or pole orders and rational and integral leading-term identities from its arithmetic cohomology? This is conditional on the Burns–Flach hypotheses on motivic cohomology, comparison maps, coefficient compatibility and coherence.

problems.title: Permanent versus Determinant over C
problems.statement: Over C, let dc(per_n) be the least m for which the n×n permanent per_n(X) equals the determinant of an m×m matrix whose entries are affine-linear forms in the n^2 variables X, as an exact polynomial identity. Assert that dc(per_n) is not O(n^c) for any real constant c>0: explicitly, for every c>0, C>0 and integer N≥1, some n≥N satisfies dc(per_n)>C*n^c. No restrictions of equivariance, sparsity or symmetry are imposed on the representing matrix. This is exact, not border, determinantal complexity over C; the selected assertion is the source’s VP_ws != VNP formulation, not an assertion that it is equivalent to VP != VNP.
problems.question: The permanent is the determinant-like sum with all permutation terms positive. If an n-by-n permanent is represented exactly as a determinant with affine-linear expressions in the original entries, must the required matrix size escape every polynomial bound in n, over the complex numbers?
problems.why: A proof would separate the permanent from polynomial-size weakly-skew algebraic computation. A polynomial-size determinant representation would refute this separation, even if no uniform algorithm for producing those representations were supplied.

problems.atlasNote: OpenAI release update, 6 October 2026: the full ranked target remains unclosed by these results. Exact scope reviewed; proofs not independently audited, refereeing not independently confirmed, and Lean artifacts not executed. Family 108: The border bound is over C and allows arbitrary affine-linear determinant representations, so it implies the same Omega(n^3) lower bound for exact determinantal complexity in the ranked model. The ranked assertion requires growth beyond every fixed polynomial n^c. A cubic bound remains polynomial and is therefore partial lower-bound progress, not permanent-versus-determinant separation. Earlier qualification retained: Permanent versus determinant remains open for unrestricted exact affine determinantal complexity over C. Quadratic lower bounds, border results and power-sum polynomials do not prove superpolynomial permanent growth; exact current-status evidence remains partly dated.

problems.title: Deligne conjecture on coefficient-equivariant critical motivic L-values
problems.statement: For every pure motive M over Q with coefficients in a number field E, in Deligne's geometric realization formalism (Betti, de Rham and compatible l-adic realizations with comparison, dual, tensor and Tate-twist structures), and every critical integer n, the normalized finite L-value vector L(M,n)/((2*pi*i)^(n*d_sign)*c^sign(M)) lies in the diagonal E inside E tensor C, where sign=(-1)^n and d_sign=dim_E H_B^sign(M). Here H_B^sign is the sign eigenspace of complex conjugation, and c^sign is the determinant of the Betti/de Rham comparison to the corresponding filtration quotient, computed in E-rational bases and defined modulo E-units as in Deligne1.7/2.6. Critical means that L_infinity(sigma,M,s) and L_infinity(sigma,Mdual,1-s) have no pole at s=n for every embedding sigma:E->C (equivalently use Mdual(1) at -s). Use finite, not completed, L-functions with the compatible E-valued local factors of2.2. Analytic continuation giving finite values at the selected critical integer and the source's well-defined compatible realizations/local factors are defining prerequisites, not assertions proved by this period law and not a restriction to cases whose continuation is already known. The simultaneous embedding vector must come from one element of E; unrelated componentwise algebraicity is insufficient. All-zero values are allowed, but mixed zero/nonzero components do not satisfy the diagonal membership. No general nonvanishing or order-of-zero assertion from Deligne2.7 is appended.
problems.question: For a pure motive over the rationals, do its critical L-values, divided by the predicted periods and powers of 2πi, come from one element of its coefficient number field across every complex embedding? This asks whether geometric periods account for these values, assuming compatible realizations and analytic continuation giving finite values at those integers.
problems.why: A proof would relate critical L-values to Betti–de Rham periods compatibly across all coefficient embeddings. The requirement is one shared algebraic element; separate algebraicity of unrelated components would not suffice.
problems.family: Deligne conjecture on coefficient-equivariant critical motivic L-values
problems.atlasNote: Deligne critical values remain open_with_solved_subcases for the coefficient-equivariant universal motive target. Recent CM-automorphic results retain regularity/rationality hypotheses; numerical checks on curves are not universal proofs.

consequences.positiveBranch: Establish the full normalized period law in its stated domain, extending beyond the reviewed restricted automorphic constructions without asserting a separate analytic or integral special-value package.
consequences.negativeBranch: Establish a failure of the exact normalized E-valued law or its simultaneous embedding compatibility, not merely an unrelated nonvanishing assertion.

problems.title: FPT versus W[1]
problems.statement: Prove or disprove FPT!=W[1] in classical uniform parameterized complexity. Equivalently, determine whether there is a deterministic algorithm, a total computable function f:N->N and an absolute constant c such that on every finite simple n-vertex graph G and every integer 1<=k<=n it decides the existence of a k-clique within f(k)n^c steps. The conjecture asserts no such algorithm. The function and exponent are fixed with the algorithm; no input-length advice, oracle or nonuniform circuit family is allowed.
problems.question: Can we deterministically decide whether an n-vertex graph contains k mutually connected vertices in time f(k)n^c, for some computable function f and fixed constant c independent of k? This would confine any non-polynomial growth in the bound to the chosen clique size k.
problems.why: Proving that no such uniform algorithm exists would separate FPT from W[1] and imply P ≠ NP. An FPT algorithm would allow arbitrary computable dependence on k, so it would not by itself give polynomial running time in the full input size.
problems.family: FPT versus W[1]
problems.atlasNote: FPT versus W[1] remains open. Yi's counting-collapse claim was explicitly withdrawn May 10, 2026; independent 2026 work retains the separation as an assumption. The ordinary uniform k-Clique target is unchanged.

consequences.positiveBranch: A separation establishes that the complete parameterized Clique problem has no allowed FPT decider and supports the usual intractability conclusions obtained via W[1]-hardness reductions.
consequences.negativeBranch: An FPT Clique algorithm transfers through W[1]-completeness reductions to all W[1] problems. Its parameter dependence may grow arbitrarily fast computably, so equality alone does not give a polynomial-time Clique algorithm in the full input size.

problems.title: The Lindeloef Hypothesis on the Growth of the Riemann Zeta Function
problems.statement: Prove that for every epsilon>0 there is a constant C_epsilon such that |zeta(1/2+it)| <= C_epsilon |t|^epsilon for all sufficiently large real |t|.
problems.question: As we move up or down the line with real part one-half, is the magnitude of the Riemann zeta function eventually bounded by every positive power of the height above or below the real axis, up to a constant depending on that power?
problems.why: A proof would rule out growth at any fixed positive power along the critical line, controlling even its unusually large values. A disproof would demonstrate repeated growth exceeding at least one such power bound.
problems.family: The Lindeloef Hypothesis on the Growth of the Riemann Zeta Function

consequences.negativeBranch: A disproof would exhibit some epsilon>0 and arbitrarily large t for which |zeta(1/2+it)| is not O(|t|^epsilon).

problems.title: Zilber-Pink Conjecture on Unlikely Intersections
problems.statement: Let S be a mixed Shimura variety and W an irreducible subvariety of S defined over C. Call a subvariety A of W atypical if there is a special subvariety T of S with A contained in the intersection of T and W and dim A > dim W + dim T - dim S. Prove that the union of all atypical subvarieties of W is a finite union of atypical subvarieties, equivalently that W contains only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties.
problems.question: Must every irreducible complex subvariety of a mixed Shimura variety contain only finitely many maximal pieces where intersection with a special subvariety is larger than dimension counting predicts? These oversized pieces are the conjecture’s atypical intersections.
problems.why: A proof would organize all these unexpectedly large intersections into finitely many maximal exceptional pieces. This would give a finite geometric description even when the variety meets infinitely many special subvarieties.
problems.family: Zilber-Pink Conjecture on Unlikely Intersections
problems.atlasNote: OpenAI release update, 6 October 2026: the full ranked target remains unclosed by these results. Exact scope reviewed; proofs not independently audited, refereeing not independently confirmed, and Lean artifacts not executed. Family 016: Theorem 1.3 of the elliptic-squares paper gives finiteness for every closed Hodge-generic curve in A_2 over Qbar, for intersections with all special subvarieties of dimension at most one. Since A_2 has dimension three, these are exactly the potentially atypical point intersections for such a curve; intersections with special surfaces have expected dimension zero, and Hodge genericity excludes the whole curve being special. Thus this is a genuine subcase of the frozen mixed-Shimura target. The abelian theorem is separately over number fields with subvarieties over their algebraic closures and torsion cosets as special subvarieties. Its normalization uses S=<X>_sp. Within that abelian setting the relative-versus-ambient issue does not invalidate the ambient analogue: if S=A the formulas coincide; if S is proper in A, X itself is ambient-atypical by taking T=S, so it is the unique inclusion-maximal ambient-atypical subvariety. This observation does not identify every abelian torsion-coset setting with the target's general mixed-Shimura setting. Neither theorem covers every complex subvariety of every mixed Shimura variety. Preserve the full target as open with these stated subcases. Earlier qualification retained: Zilber–Pink remains open_with_solved_subcases for the full mixed-Shimura target. Strong non-Qbar/Hodge-generic hypotheses and pure-Shimura cases do not cover it; current universal mixed-scope certification remains limited.

consequences.positiveBranch: A positive resolution would leave only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties in every irreducible W inside a mixed Shimura variety.
consequences.negativeBranch: A negative resolution would exhibit a W containing infinitely many maximal atypical subvarieties.

problems.title: Campana's Conjecture Characterizing Special Varieties by Potential Density of Rational Points
problems.statement: For every number field K and every smooth projective geometrically integral variety X/K, prove or disprove that X over an algebraic closure of K is special in Campana's sense if and only if X(L) is Zariski dense in X for some finite extension L/K. Here specialness has its usual projective meaning: for each integer 1<=p<=dim X and rank-one coherent subsheaf F of the sheaf of algebraic p-forms on X over the algebraic closure, the Kodaira dimension kappa(F) is less than p (equivalently, the Campana core is a point). A proof must establish the biconditional for all such X; one counterexample to either implication refutes it. This target excludes nonproper integral-point, weakly-special, analytic and function-field variants.
problems.question: For a smooth projective geometrically integral variety over a number field, is Campana's geometric condition of specialness exactly what allows its rational points to become Zariski dense after a finite extension of the field? Specialness is tested over the algebraic closure.
problems.why: This would characterize an arithmetic property—potential density of rational points—by geometry. A proof would also give potential density for K3 surfaces and the Bombieri–Lang non-density assertion for positive-dimensional varieties of general type.
problems.family: Campana specialness and rational points
problems.atlasNote: The December 2025 Bartsch–Javanpeykar–Levin paper states that neither implication is known in full generality, and March 2026 discussion retains the arithmetic conjecture while separating weak specialness and geometric results.

consequences.positiveBranch: A proof would characterize arithmetic potential density geometrically, imply potential density for all K3 surfaces over number fields, and imply Bombieri–Lang non-density for positive-dimensional varieties of general type.
consequences.negativeBranch: A counterexample would separate arithmetic potential density from Campana specialness in at least one direction; it would not automatically refute the K3 or Bombieri–Lang assertions.

problems.title: Weight–Monodromy Conjecture
problems.statement: Let K be ANY nonarchimedean local field with finite residue field F_q of characteristic p, X ANY proper smooth variety over K, i>=0, and l ANY prime different from p. Put V=H^i_et(X_over_Kbar,Qbar_l), retaining the original K. On an open inertia subgroup the action is unipotent and defines nilpotent monodromy N:V->V(-1), with its Galois-equivariant Tate twist. Let M be the unique increasing monodromy filtration centred at zero: N(M_j) is contained in M_(j-2)(-1), and N^a:gr^M_a(V)->gr^M_(-a)(V)(-a) is an isomorphism for every a>=0. For EVERY integer j and ANY lift Phi of geometric Frobenius of F_q, every eigenvalue alpha on gr^M_j(V) is conjectured to be algebraic and have absolute value q^((i+j)/2) under ALL complex embeddings. This is purity of weight i+j. Defining N on an open inertia subgroup does not replace K or q. Finite-extension proof reductions must change cardinality and Frobenius consistently. Extending l-adic coefficients does not change the target. The equivalent source convention compares zero-centred M_j with W_(i+j); weight-filtration existence is not an added unresolved assertion. No restriction to projective, semistable, geometrically connected or special complete-intersection varieties is imposed. l=p, crystalline, torsion and arbitrary rigid-analytic analogues are not substituted.
problems.question: Monodromy organizes a variety’s l-adic cohomology into layers. Are the Frobenius eigenvalues on each layer algebraic, with the absolute sizes predicted by its degree and layer index in every complex embedding, for every smooth proper variety over a nonarchimedean local field and every prime l different from the residue characteristic?
problems.why: A proof would force every such eigenvalue to have absolute value q^((i + j)/2) under every complex embedding. It would link local monodromy to prescribed Frobenius weights without imposing projectivity or semistability.
problems.family: Weight–Monodromy Conjecture
problems.atlasNote: Weight–monodromy remains open_with_solved_subcases. Complete intersections in abelian varieties are a subcase, and 2026 formality work assumes weight–monodromy. Rigid-analytic counterexamples or l=p analogues are not the frozen smooth proper algebraic l != p statement.

consequences.positiveBranch: Establish universal prescribed Frobenius weights on monodromy-graded proper-smooth cohomology.
consequences.negativeBranch: Establish failure of the proposed universal local monodromy-purity relation.

problems.title: Sarnak's Mobius randomness conjecture for zero-entropy systems
problems.statement: Prove that for every compact metric topological dynamical system (X,T) of zero topological entropy, every continuous f on X, and every x in X, the average N^(-1) sum_{n<=N} mu(n) f(T^n x) tends to zero as N tends to infinity.
problems.question: The Möbius function is zero on integers divisible by a prime square, and otherwise is +1 or −1 according to the parity of the number of prime factors. Does it have zero average correlation with every continuous measurement along every orbit of a compact metric dynamical system with zero topological entropy?
problems.why: A proof would exclude persistent correlation between the Möbius function and any observable orbit in this entire zero-entropy class. A counterexample would locate structured dynamical behavior with a surviving arithmetic correlation.
problems.family: Sarnak's Mobius randomness conjecture for zero-entropy systems
problems.atlasNote: Sarnak remains open for ordinary n-iterate Cesaro averages. Polynomial-iterate counterexamples and a special infinite-torus theorem do not resolve it. An author-site disproof assertion lacks a verified exact counterexample or independent acceptance.

consequences.positiveBranch: A proof would establish Mobius orthogonality for every zero-entropy topological orbit and every continuous observable under the stated normalization.
consequences.negativeBranch: A disproof would exhibit a zero-entropy system, continuous observable, and orbit whose Mobius-weighted averages do not converge to zero.

problems.title: Deligne's Absolute Hodge Conjecture
problems.statement: For every smooth projective variety X over C, every p>=0 and every rational Hodge class alpha in H^(2p)(X,Q(p)), alpha is absolute Hodge: for every automorphism sigma of C, its sigma-conjugate under algebraic de Rham comparison on X^sigma is again a rational Hodge class, with the same Tate-twist convention.
problems.question: Hodge classes are cohomology classes singled out by a variety's complex geometry. On every smooth projective complex variety, must each rational Hodge class remain one after any automorphism of the complex number field?
problems.why: A proof would make the Hodge property invariant under all these field automorphisms, using the specified de Rham comparison and Tate twist. A counterexample would identify a class whose conjugate loses that property.
problems.family: Hodge conjectures
problems.atlasNote: OpenAI release update, 6 October 2026: the full ranked target remains unclosed by these results. Exact scope reviewed; proofs not independently audited, refereeing not independently confirmed, and Lean artifacts not executed. Family 032: Algebraic cycle classes remain rational Hodge classes under conjugation, so algebraicity supplies the absolute-Hodge assertion on the complex projective K3 products and other explicitly covered varieties. This is a mathematical consequence restricted to those classes of varieties, not a proof that every Hodge class on every smooth projective complex variety is absolute. Earlier qualification retained: Supported as conjectural by the 2025 scholarly survey, with abelian varieties established; no exhaustive certification or endorsement of unscreened proof claims.

consequences.positiveBranch: A proof would establish stability of rational Hodge classes under all complex-field automorphisms.
consequences.negativeBranch: A counterexample would refute that stability and, because algebraic classes are absolute, also refute the ordinary Hodge conjecture.

problems.title: Elliott-Halberstam Conjecture on the Level of Distribution of Primes
problems.statement: Prove that for every A > 0 and every 0 < theta < 1, the sum over q <= x^theta of the maximal Chebyshev error |psi(y; q, a) - y/phi(q)| over y <= x and (a,q)=1 is O(x / (log x)^A), extending Bombieri-Vinogradov from theta < 1/2 to every theta < 1.
problems.question: When counting primes in arithmetic progressions, can their distribution errors be controlled for step sizes nearly as large as the counting limit x? Elliott–Halberstam predicts arbitrarily strong logarithmic savings in the sum of the largest errors over residue classes and shorter counting ranges, for step sizes up to x^θ with any 0 < θ < 1.
problems.why: A proof would control the combined error in prime distribution across arithmetic progressions for moduli extending to every fixed power below x. The estimate controls the sum of worst errors for each modulus, retaining uniformity over shorter cutoffs.
problems.family: Elliott-Halberstam Conjecture on the Level of Distribution of Primes
problems.atlasNote: Elliott–Halberstam remains open unconditionally. A recent implication assumes both GRH and Dirichlet-L pair correlation, while restricted-modulus results do not prove the frozen all-moduli maximal-error estimate.

consequences.positiveBranch: Would prove that for every A > 0 and every 0 < theta < 1, the sum over q <= x^theta of the maximal Chebyshev error |psi(y; q, a) - y/phi(q)| over y <= x and (a,q)=1 is O(x / (log x)^A), extending Bombieri-Vinogradov from theta < 1/2 to every theta < 1.
consequences.negativeBranch: Would exhibit a counterexample or obstruction to the assertion that for every A > 0 and every 0 < theta < 1, the sum over q <= x^theta of the maximal Chebyshev error |psi(y; q, a) - y/phi(q)| over y <= x and (a,q)=1 is O(x / (log x)^A), extending Bombieri-Vinogradov from theta < 1/2 to every theta < 1.

problems.title: The Mumford-Tate Conjecture for Abelian Varieties over Number Fields
problems.statement: Prove that for every abelian variety A over a number field K, the Lie algebra of the l-adic Galois image Lie(Gal(Kbar/K)) equals the Lie algebra of the Mumford-Tate group MT(A) tensor Q_l.
problems.question: An abelian variety has symmetries seen through both number theory and complex geometry. Over any number field, do the Lie algebras of its l-adic Galois image and its Mumford–Tate group agree after passing to l-adic coefficients, so that the two descriptions give the same infinitesimal symmetries?
problems.why: A proof would identify the specified arithmetic Galois symmetries with the Mumford–Tate description at the Lie-algebra level. A counterexample would expose a mismatch between these two symmetry measurements for an abelian variety.
problems.family: The Mumford-Tate Conjecture for Abelian Varieties over Number Fields

consequences.negativeBranch: A negative resolution would exhibit an abelian variety for which those Lie algebras differ.

problems.title: Grothendieck–Teichmüller Conjecture
problems.statement: Let G_Q=Gal(Qbar/Q). Let GT-hat be Drinfeld's original profinite Grothendieck-Teichmuller group, including its standard commutator and invertibility conditions, not merely the pair-equation monoid, gentle GT, a pro-l or prounipotent version, or a higher-genus subgroup. Fix the standard Ihara embedding Ih:G_Q -> GT-hat specified by the Ihara splitting in Bortnovskyi-Dolgushev-Holikov-Pashkovskyi Section1.3, equations1.5-1.6: Ih(g)=((chi(g)-1)/2,f_g) in that source's coordinates, with chi the cyclotomic character, and associated action x -> x^chi(g), y -> f_g^(-1)y^chi(g)f_g on the profinite free group. The conjecture asserts that this actual continuous injective homomorphism is surjective, hence an isomorphism of profinite groups. The source's group law and fixed splitting are retained; formulas from an opposite composition convention are not mixed into this definition.
problems.question: The absolute Galois group of the rationals describes the field symmetries of algebraic numbers. Does its standard Ihara embedding account for every element of Drinfeld’s original profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group, which encodes compatible symmetries of fundamental-group data?
problems.why: Surjectivity would identify that entire profinite group with the arithmetic Galois group through the actual embedding. Failure would exhibit elements satisfying the group’s defining conditions that do not arise from Galois symmetries.
problems.family: Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory
problems.atlasNote: Grothendieck–Teichmuller remains open for surjectivity of the fixed Ihara embedding into the original full profinite GT. August 2026 quotient results and underlying-space homeomorphisms do not prove this group-homomorphism surjectivity.

consequences.positiveBranch: Identify every element of the original profinite GT as arising under the actual absolute-Galois embedding.
consequences.negativeBranch: Establish that the original profinite GT contains genuinely nongalois elements, delimiting that group-theoretic reconstruction criterion.

problems.title: PSPACE versus EXPTIME
problems.statement: Determine whether PSPACE=EXPTIME for languages over finite binary strings in the standard deterministic multitape Turing-machine model with a read-only input tape and work tapes. PSPACE is the union over integers k>=1 of DSPACE(n^k), with asymptotic constant factors allowed and read-only input cells not counted as work space. EXPTIME is the union over integers k>=1 of DTIME(2^(n^k)), with asymptotic constant factors allowed. Machines are total deciders that halt on every input. This is an unrelativized equality of the full classes, not of one fixed resource exponent.
problems.question: If a deterministic algorithm solves a yes-or-no problem in time 2^(n^k) for some fixed k, must another deterministic algorithm solve it using only polynomially many working-memory bits in the input length n?
problems.why: An equality would show that polynomial memory suffices for every computation in the full exponential-time class. A separation would identify a decision problem whose time bound can be exponential but whose memory requirements exceed every polynomial.
problems.family: PSPACE versus EXPTIME
problems.atlasNote: PSPACE versus EXPTIME remains open with bounded recency evidence. The Czerwinski separation was withdrawn in March 2024 with an independent critique, which defeats that claim but does not certify absence of every later one.

consequences.positiveBranch: Equality would place every deterministic exponential-time decision problem within polynomial work space, though not necessarily polynomial time. This follows directly from the fixed class definitions and the known inclusion.
consequences.negativeBranch: Strict containment would establish an exponential-time-decidable language requiring more than every polynomial work-space bound, resolving this specific time-versus-space boundary without automatically settling other class separations.

problems.title: Grothendieck Standard Conjecture of Hodge Type
problems.statement: For every smooth projective irreducible variety X of dimension n over an algebraically closed field k of any characteristic and every ample divisor class L, put N^i(X)_Q equal to codimension-i algebraic cycles with rational coefficients modulo numerical equivalence, with N^j=0 outside 0<=j<=n. For each integer 0<=i<=n/2 let P_L^i=ker(L^(n-2i+1):N^i(X)_Q -> N^(n-i+1)(X)_Q). The numerical standard conjecture of Hodge type asserts that q_L^i(a,b)=(-1)^i deg(a.b.L^(n-2i)) is positive definite on P_L^i after extending scalars to R. This is numerical primitive positivity, not an unconditional identification with primitive algebraic cohomology for an arbitrary Weil theory; it does not assume or require proving the other standard conjectures separately.
problems.question: After identifying algebraic cycles with the same intersection numbers, does the sign-corrected intersection form give a positive value on every nonzero primitive class? This is asked in codimensions up to half the dimension, for every ample class on smooth projective irreducible varieties over algebraically closed fields of any characteristic.
problems.why: A proof would give a positive inner-product structure to these primitive numerical cycle spaces. The conclusion concerns cycles modulo numerical equivalence and does not itself identify them with primitive classes in an arbitrary cohomology theory.
problems.family: Grothendieck’s standard conjectures
problems.atlasNote: OpenAI release update, 6 October 2026: the full ranked target remains unclosed by these results. Exact scope reviewed; proofs not independently audited, refereeing not independently confirmed, and Lean artifacts not executed. Family 032: The stated consequence is the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic. This supplies the abelian-variety part of the ranked numerical primitive-positivity question. Its universal quantifier over smooth projective irreducible varieties remains wider, even though the characteristic range of the abelian consequence is unrestricted. Earlier qualification retained: Standard Conjecture of Hodge type remains open_with_solved_subcases. Fourfolds, powers of threefolds and other specified examples do not establish numerical primitive positivity in every dimension and characteristic; newer preprint proofs were not independently certified.

consequences.positiveBranch: Settle the numerical Hodge-index positivity law for primitive algebraic cycles in the exact all-characteristic scope.
consequences.negativeBranch: Establish a failure of the numerical primitive positivity law, identifying a limitation of that assertion without automatically resolving another standard conjecture.

problems.title: Kannan-Lovasz-Simonovits conjecture on isoperimetry of log-concave measures
problems.statement: Prove that there is a universal constant C > 0 such that, for every log-concave probability measure mu on R^n, its Cheeger isoperimetric constant is at least C times the infimum of mu^+(H)/min(mu(H), 1-mu(H)) over halfspaces H. Equivalently, prove the dimension-free KLS lower bound psi_mu >= C/sqrt(||Cov(mu)||_op), with a universal constant C.
problems.question: For a log-concave probability distribution, can a hyperplane cut achieve a boundary-to-mass ratio within a universal constant factor of the best possible cut, in every dimension? Each cut’s boundary is normalized by the smaller of the two masses it separates.
problems.why: A proof would make simple halfspace cuts sufficient, up to a universal factor, to describe the measure’s worst isoperimetric bottleneck. The bound would remain independent of dimension and admit the stated covariance formulation.
problems.family: Kannan-Lovasz-Simonovits conjecture on isoperimetry of log-concave measures
