problems.title: Strongly Polynomial Linear Programming
problems.statement: Does a uniform deterministic algorithm solve every rational LP max c^T x, Ax <= b, x >= 0, returning an exact optimum or correctly reporting infeasibility or unboundedness, with poly(m,n) exact arithmetic operations and comparisons independent of coefficient encoding lengths and polynomial intermediate representation size in the binary input length? Operations on input and intermediate rationals are addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and comparison. For a stored p/q with q positive, size is ceil(log2(abs(p)+1)) + ceil(log2(q+1)); reduction to coprime terms, floor and bit extraction are not free operations. No nonuniform advice or arbitrary real constants are allowed. The displayed form is without loss under strongly polynomial slack-variable and variable-splitting reductions. This is the deterministic formulation; a randomized algorithm alone does not settle it.
problems.question: Can every rational linear program be solved deterministically using a number of exact arithmetic operations bounded by a polynomial in the numbers of variables and constraints, independently of the coefficient lengths?
problems.why: Linear programming is central to optimization. A strongly polynomial algorithm would separate its arithmetic complexity from the size of its coefficients, while also keeping intermediate number representations polynomial in the binary input length.
problems.family: Strongly polynomial linear programming and simplex methods

The failed claim is evidence history, not a separate disputed public status.

consequences.negativeBranch: An impossibility theorem would rule out this arithmetic/bit-size specification for general rational LP, separating it from known weakly polynomial solvability while leaving existing algorithms and structured strongly polynomial subcases valid.

problems.statement: Let K be a global field (a number field or the function field of a curve over a finite field), G an absolutely almost simple simply connected algebraic K-group, and S a finite nonempty set of places of K containing every archimedean place when K is a number field. problems.question: Can an ordinary computer efficiently check any efficient quantum computation by exchanging classical messages with one quantum prover, reliably accepting correct answers and rejecting false ones even if a cheating prover has unlimited computing power?
problems.why: An affirmative answer would give purely classical verification of every computation in BQP while requiring only an efficient honest quantum prover. The guarantee would resist computationally unbounded cheating without relying on cryptographic hardness assumptions.
problems.family: Unconditional Single-Prover Classical Verification of BQP Computations

problems.title: Existence of a Length-Optimal Propositional Proof System
problems.statement: Does there exist a polynomial-time computable function P from finite binary strings onto the encodings of all propositional tautologies such that, for every polynomial-time computable function Q onto the same tautologies, there is a polynomial q_Q for which every Q-proof pi has some P-proof sigma with P(sigma)=Q(pi) and |sigma| <= q_Q(|pi|)? The polynomial may depend on Q. No polynomial-time algorithm for finding sigma from pi is required. This is the ordinary unrelativized Cook–Reckhow setting without advice or randomness; resolve existence or nonexistence of such P.
problems.question: Is there a Cook–Reckhow propositional proof system whose shortest proofs are at most polynomially longer than those in any other such system, with the polynomial allowed to depend on the other system? An efficient way to translate proofs is not required.
problems.why: This asks whether one proof system can match every other system in proof length. It separates the existence of short proofs from the algorithmic task of finding or translating them.
problems.family: Optimal propositional proof systems
problems.atlasNote: Egidy’s2026 ICALP paper explicitly leaves ordinary TAUT optimality open; its recursive-jump and oracle results do not settle the unrelativized existence question.

consequences.positiveBranch: There would be a single propositional proof system that is at least polynomially as succinct as each competitor; neither efficient proof search nor efficient translation from competing systems is implied.
consequences.negativeBranch: No propositional proof system would dominate all competitors in proof length up to polynomial overhead; this would also rule out p-optimal systems and polynomially bounded systems, hence imply NP differs from coNP by the Cook–Reckhow criterion.

problems.statement: Prove or disprove that MCSP is NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions, where an input is the truth table of a Boolean function and a size bound and asks whether a circuit of at most that size computes the function.

problems.title: Hyperlinearity of Every Group
problems.statement: Determine whether every group G is hyperlinear. Precisely, for each finite F contained in G and each epsilon>0, must there be d>=1 and phi:F->U(d) such that ||phi(g)phi(h)-phi(gh)||_(2,d)<epsilon whenever g,h,gh belong to F, and ||phi(g)-I||_(2,d)>sqrt(2)-epsilon for every nonidentity g in F? Here ||X||_(2,d)=(Tr(X*X)/d)^(1/2) is the normalized Hilbert-Schmidt norm. A negative resolution is a group failing this condition.
problems.question: Can every finite piece of any group's multiplication table be modeled arbitrarily accurately by unitary matrices, while nonidentity elements stay separated from the identity in the normalized Hilbert–Schmidt distance?
problems.why: A proof would give finite-dimensional unitary approximations for every group in the precise stated sense. A counterexample would identify a finite pattern and tolerance for which the required approximation and separation cannot coexist.
problems.family: Group approximation and determinants
problems.atlasNote: Direct scholarly status is explicit through the 23 June 2026 revision; targeted searches through 11 September 2026 found no verified group counterexample. This is a bounded source review, not exhaustive expert certification.

consequences.positiveBranch: A positive resolution establishes the stated normalized-unitary approximation property for every group.
consequences.negativeBranch: A negative resolution supplies a non-hyperlinear group, which must also be nonsofic by the established sofic-to-hyperlinear implication.

problems.title: Torsion Conjecture for Abelian Varieties of Dimension at Least Two
problems.statement: For every integer g>=2 and every number field K, there exists a finite constant B(g,K) such that every abelian variety A defined over K of dimension g satisfies #A(K)_tors <= B(g,K). Here A(K)_tors is the subgroup of K-rational torsion points. The bound is uniform over all such A, without dependence on A, its height, endomorphisms, polarization degree or reduction type; it may depend on g and K. No effective formula, explicit numerical value or classification of torsion groups is required.
problems.question: After fixing a number field and a dimension of at least two, is there one common bound on the number of finite-order points defined over that field on any abelian variety of that dimension?
problems.why: A proof would prevent rational torsion from growing arbitrarily large while dimension and field remain fixed. The bound could exist without an explicit formula or a classification of the possible torsion groups.
problems.family: Torsion Conjecture for Abelian Varieties of Dimension at Least Two
problems.atlasNote: The August2026 Gao–Gu introduction and January2026 Ji–Song–Xie explicitly leave the higher-dimensional assertion open. Gao–Gu's unconditional number-field estimate still depends on the variety and its full-looking uniform statement is conditional/semistable; Looper–Yap works over a characteristic-zero function field with no isotrivial part. These are not unconditional solutions of the selected all-number-field target; bounded search is not an exhaustive status certificate. The displayed status is retained from the selected, previously reviewed input, with its bound qualifications; no fresh current-status certification is claimed here.

consequences.positiveBranch: For every fixed g,K, all possible torsion-cardinalities would be bounded independently of A. Applying the full assertion over Q to Res(K/Q)A of dimension g[K:Q] yields a bound depending only on g and field degree. No explicit formula, classification, height lower bound, Lang–Silverman result or cryptographic break is implied by this review.
consequences.negativeBranch: A fixed-g,fixed-K family with unbounded rational torsion would refute the selected assertion. Equivalently, a rigorously transported fixed-degree witness may refute it over Q in a higher fixed dimension. This would not refute the solved g=1 case or function-field theorems with different hypotheses.

problems.title: Global Gan–Gross–Prasad Conjecture (Fixed-Representation Form)
problems.statement: For every number field F, let E be F, a quadratic extension, or F×F, and let W⊂V be a nondegenerate relevant pair with form sign epsilon, split W-perp, and epsilon*(-1)^dim(W-perp)=-1; a two-dimensional orthogonal V or W is required to be nonsplit. Use exactly the groups, covers, Bessel/Fourier–Jacobi representation nu and auxiliary data of Gan–Gross–Prasad Section 23, and R of Section 24, including the skew-hermitian character mu and its matching inverse twist in R. For every irreducible tempered representation pi occurring with multiplicity one in the cuspidal automorphic spectrum, Conjecture 24.1 asserts: the global period F(nu) is nonzero on pi if and only if Hom_H(F_v)(pi_v,nu_v) is nonzero for every place v and L(pi,R,1/2) is nonzero. Quantification is over all data permitted there, including relevant orthogonal, hermitian, symplectic/metaplectic and skew-hermitian cases. This is the fixed-representation equivalence, not the refined period identity or packet-existence formulation.
problems.question: For a fixed tempered cuspidal automorphic representation in the Gan–Gross–Prasad setting of classical groups and their covers, with multiplicity one, is its global period nonzero exactly when every local compatibility test succeeds and its associated L-function has a nonzero central value?
problems.why: The equivalence would decide global period nonvanishing from local representation data and one central L-value. It would connect these arithmetic and representation-theoretic tests for each fixed representation, without asserting a refined formula for the period's size.
problems.family: Global Gan–Gross–Prasad Conjecture (Fixed-Representation Form)

consequences.positiveBranch: A proof supplies a uniform local-and-L-value criterion for global period nonvanishing across the selected classical groups, linking automorphic representation theory to arithmetic invariants.
consequences.negativeBranch: A counterexample identifies a failure of that proposed local-to-global criterion and forces a revision of its scope or governing data, without itself disproving every refinement or neighboring conjecture.

problems.title: Planted Clique Conjecture
problems.statement: For every fixed real alpha with 0<alpha<1/2, set k_n=floor(n^(1/2-alpha)). Sample a uniform k_n-subset S of n labeled vertices, put every edge inside S, and independently include each other edge with probability1/2. There is no randomized algorithm running in time polynomial in n that, given this graph, outputs exactly S with probability tending to1 as n tends to infinity, over S, remaining edges and its internal coins. Algorithms may depend on the fixed alpha but receive no advice depending on n.
problems.question: Hide a complete subgraph on about n^(1/2−α) randomly chosen vertices in an otherwise random n-vertex graph whose edges appear independently with probability 1/2. For every fixed 0<α<1/2, is recovering all hidden vertices with probability tending to one impossible in randomized polynomial time?
problems.why: A proof would establish a computational barrier to recovering the actual planted vertex set in this random-graph model. An algorithm refuting it would need exact recovery for some fixed exponent, rather than merely detecting that a clique was planted.
problems.family: Planted Clique Conjecture
problems.atlasNote: Hirahara--Shimizu and Meka--Potechin--Wigderson retain the unrestricted sub-square-root recovery question while providing restricted-model context. A recent hypergraph matrix-observation result surfaced in the bounded root query is a different model and square-root regime, not a resolution of this exact assertion. The disposition is qualified open, not worldwide claim absence. The displayed status is retained from the selected, previously reviewed input, with its bound qualifications; no fresh current-status certification is claimed here.

consequences.positiveBranch: Prove that for EVERY fixed0<alpha<1/2 and EVERY in-scope randomized polynomial-time recovery algorithm its exact-recovery success probability does NOT tend to1.
consequences.negativeBranch: Prove that for SOME fixed0<alpha<1/2 an in-scope randomized polynomial-time algorithm recovers exactly the planted set with probability tending to1. An existence proof suffices without prescribing a code artifact; a detection-only or different-distribution result requires a checked transfer.

problems.title: Superlinear Circuit Lower Bounds for Explicit Boolean Functions
problems.statement: There exists a Boolean function family f_n:{0,1}^n->{0,1}, n>=1, evaluated by a single deterministic polynomial-time algorithm on (1^n,x), whose minimum gate count C_B2(f_n) over single-output fan-in-two circuits using arbitrary binary Boolean gates satisfies C_B2(f_n)=omega(n): for every c>0 there is N such that C_B2(f_n)>c*n for every n>=N. The circuits have unrestricted depth and fan-out; no fixed linear constant counts as superlinear.
problems.question: Can a family of yes-or-no functions be computable in polynomial time yet require circuits whose number of two-input gates grows faster than any constant times the input length, even with unrestricted depth and fan-out?
problems.why: A proof would exhibit an efficiently specified computation whose circuit size grows faster than every linear bound. The eventual growth requirement excludes merely improving a fixed constant in front of n or obtaining lower bounds at isolated input lengths.

problems.title: Uniform Subconvexity for Standard Automorphic L-Functions on GL(n)
problems.statement: For every integer n≥1 and every number field F, there exist constants δ(n,F)>0 and A(n,F)>0 such that |L(1/2,π)|≤A(n,F) C(π)^(1/4−δ(n,F)) for every unitary cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n(A_F), where L(s,π) is the standard finite-part L-function and C(π) its analytic conductor. The bound must be uniform simultaneously in all finite and archimedean parameters of π; imaginary unitary twists are included. Any fixed positive exponent saving suffices; the optimal exponent is not requested.
problems.question: An L-function’s analytic conductor measures its arithmetic and analytic complexity. For each fixed rank n and number field, are the magnitudes of the central values at s = 1/2 of all unitary cuspidal standard L-functions on GL(n) bounded by a constant times the conductor raised to an exponent strictly below one-quarter, uniformly as all parameters vary together?
problems.why: A proof would give a uniform power-saving bound for central automorphic L-values at every fixed rank and number field, even when all arithmetic and analytic parameters vary together. A disproof would rule out any such saving in at least one of these families and contradict the corresponding generalized Lindelöf prediction.
problems.family: Uniform Subconvexity for Standard Automorphic L-Functions on GL(n)
problems.atlasNote: Open with solved subcases. A level-aspect theorem for symmetric squares does not settle the arbitrary-rank all-aspect target.

consequences.positiveBranch: A proof would provide unconditional uniform power-saving control of central standard automorphic L-values in all parameters at each fixed rank and number field.
consequences.negativeBranch: A refutation would show that no positive uniform power saving is possible in some fixed-rank, fixed-field family and would contradict the corresponding generalized Lindelöf prediction.

problems.title: Murre's Chow-Kunneth Conjectures
problems.statement: For every smooth projective irreducible complex variety X of dimension d, let CH^j(X)_Q denote cycles modulo rational equivalence, with Betti Q-cohomology. A correspondence pi in CH^d(X x X)_Q acts by pi_*(a)=(p_2)_*(p_1^*(a).pi). Murre's full A-D package asserts: (A) there exists a Chow-Kunneth decomposition, namely mutually orthogonal composition-idempotents pi_0,...,pi_(2d) in CH^d(X x X)_Q summing to the diagonal and inducing projection onto H^i(X,Q) for pi_i; (B) for EVERY such decomposition and 0<=j<=d, pi_i acts as zero on CH^j when i<j or i>2j; (C) for EVERY such decomposition define F^r CH^j as the intersection of ker(pi_i)_* for max(0,2j-r+1)<=i<=2j, r>=0, with empty intersection F^0=CH^j; these filtrations are equal for ALL decompositions satisfying A; (D) for EVERY such decomposition, F^1 CH^j equals ker(CH^j(X)_Q -> H^(2j)(X,Q)). problems.title: Voevodsky's Smash-Nilpotence Conjecture
problems.statement: For every field k, every smooth projective k-variety X of dimension d, every integer 0<=r<=d, and every class alpha in CH^r(X)_Q (codimension-r cycles modulo rational equivalence with rational coefficients), assume deg(alpha.beta)=0 for every beta in CH^(d-r)(X)_Q. Voevodsky's smash-nilpotence assertion is that there exists an integer N>=1, depending on alpha, for which the N-fold EXTERNAL product alpha times ... times alpha is zero in CH^(Nr)(X^N)_Q, where X^N is the fibre product over k. No algebraic-closure, characteristic-zero or geometric-connectedness hypothesis is imposed; disconnected smooth projective schemes are interpreted on their pure-dimensional components. The reverse implication, smash-nilpotent implies numerically trivial, is known, so this is equality of numerical and smash equivalence for rational cycles. Neither intersection powers on X, composition powers of correspondences, integral coefficients, nor a uniform or computable exponent replaces this assertion.

problems.why: A proof would characterize numerical triviality by actual vanishing after enough external products. The required exponent may depend on the cycle, and the products take place on powers of the variety rather than within the original variety.

problems.title: Inhomogeneous Landau–Coulomb Global Regularity (HST All-Moment Data)
problems.statement: Fix a positive physical constant a. On [0,infinity) times R^3_x times R^3_v consider the classical Landau equation (partial_t+v dot grad_x)f=Q(f,f), where Q(f,f)=div_v integral_{R^3} A(v-w)[f(t,x,w) grad_v f(t,x,v)-f(t,x,v) grad_w f(t,x,w)]dw and A(z)=a |z|^(-1)(I-z tensor z/|z|^2) for z!=0. For every nonnegative initial datum f_0 on R^6 with f_0 in the global Holder space C^alpha for some 0<alpha<1, sup_{x,v}<v>^k f_0(x,v)<infinity for every k>=0, and constants delta,r_0,R>0 such that for every x there exists |v_x|<R with f_0>=delta on the Euclidean R^6 ball B_{r_0}(x,v_x), does the classical solution branch constructed in HST Theorems 1.2–1.4 have maximal continuation time T_E=infinity? Here <v>=(1+|v|^2)^(1/2); the branch matches f_0 as t decreases to zero, is smooth for positive time, and has all polynomial velocity weights bounded on every finite time slab of its existence. The exact question is global extension of that branch, with the sufficiently decaying uniformly continuous kinetic weak uniqueness convention in HST Section 5, not uniqueness among all generalized weak solutions. The HST Coulomb continuation quantity is Psi(T)=esssup_{0<=t<=T,x} integral f(t,x,v)dv + esssup_{0<=t<=T,x,v} f(t,x,v). Finite Psi on every finite time slab is the associated continuation criterion, not an extra hypothesis presumed true. No smallness near equilibrium, finite total spatial mass or uniform bound across different initial data is imposed.

problems.title: Kimura–O'Sullivan Finite-Dimensionality Conjecture
problems.statement: For every field k and every smooth projective variety X over k, the Chow motive h(X) with rational coefficients in the ordinary symmetric, pseudo-abelian category CHM(k)_Q is Kimura–O'Sullivan finite-dimensional: there exist motives M+ and M− and positive integers n,m such that h(X) is isomorphic to M+ direct-sum M−, the exterior power Λ^n(M+) is zero, and the symmetric power Sym^m(M−) is zero. The summands may be zero. The field k is unrestricted; characteristic zero applies to the rational coefficient field, not to k. No effective construction, uniform n,m or classification is required.

consequences.positiveBranch: Every admissible h(X) would split into even and odd finite-dimensional parts. problems.title: Palis finite-attractor full-basin density conjecture
problems.statement: For every compact connected boundaryless smooth manifold M and every finite integer r >= 1, prove the conjunction of the following two density assertions: (i) in Diff^r(M) with its C^r topology there is a dense subset D whose elements f have finitely many attractors whose basins of attraction together cover M up to a set of smooth-volume measure zero; (ii) the same holds in the space X^r(M) of C^r vector fields with its C^r topology, for the attractors and basins of the generated flows. Attractor follows Palis (2005) Sections 2.1 and 2.3: a compact invariant set A that is transitive (has a dense orbit) and attracts a set of positive volume, its basin being the set of points whose forward orbit (or forward flow trajectory) converges to A. The finite number of attractors may depend on the element of D; no uniform bound is required. Volume-zero is independent of the choice of smooth positive density on M. This is the first bullet of Palis's Global Conjecture only; physical measures, stochastic stability, metric stability under parameter perturbation, and one-dimensional-family statements are separate conjectures not included.

problems.title: Perfect-Matching Search in Deterministic NC (General Graphs)
problems.statement: Assert the existence of one logspace-uniform family (C_n) of deterministic Boolean AND/OR/NOT circuits which, for every n>=1 and every finite simple undirected graph G on labelled vertices 1,...,n given by its n-by-n adjacency matrix, outputs a perfect matching of G if one exists and outputs a distinguished NO flag if none exists. Matching output is an n-by-n edge-indicator matrix, required to encode disjoint edges covering every vertex and belonging to G; its bits are ignored when NO is output. Circuit size is bounded by C n^c and depth by C (log(n+2))^k for constants C,c,k independent of n and G, and AND/OR fan-in is at most two. A deterministic logspace transducer on unary 1^n outputs the complete circuit description, including all designated outputs. This fixes ordinary logspace-uniform NC for the multi-output search relation. It does not conflate a search algorithm with an unweighted decision algorithm or restrict the input to bipartite or planar graphs.
problems.question: Can a deterministic parallel algorithm find a perfect matching—disjoint edges covering every vertex—or report that none exists in any finite simple undirected graph, using polynomially many processors and time polynomial in log n? The algorithm must have a logspace-uniform circuit description.
problems.why: A positive answer would give a uniform parallel algorithm that constructs the matching itself without randomness. A negative answer would establish a limitation on search in this precise circuit model.

problems.title: MAJORITY is not in ACC0
problems.statement: Let MAJORITY_n(x)=1 exactly when sum_i x_i>=n/2. Define nonuniform ACC0 as Boolean families computed, for every input length n>=1, by circuits of polynomial size and some fixed constant depth using unbounded-fan-in AND, OR and MOD_m gates and fan-in-one NOT gates, with constants allowed and one fixed integer modulus m>=2 across all lengths; MOD_m outputs1 exactly when the input sum is divisible by m. problems.title: Dynamical Mordell–Lang Conjecture
problems.statement: For every field K of characteristic zero, every quasiprojective variety X over K, every K-morphism f:X->X, every closed K-subvariety V of X and every point x in X(K), the set {n in Z_{≥0}: f^n(x) is in V(K)} is a finite union of arithmetic progressions {a+bm:m in Z_{≥0}} with a,b nonnegative integers. A zero step b=0 permits a singleton, and an empty union permits no returns. All iterates are defined because f is a morphism. No dominance, etaleness, smoothness, automorphism or degree restriction is imposed.
problems.question: Repeatedly apply an algebraic map to a point and record when its orbit lands in a fixed algebraic subvariety. In characteristic zero, are these return times always a finite union of arithmetic progressions and isolated times, for every everywhere-defined map of a quasiprojective variety?
problems.why: A proof would force these orbit-intersection times to follow finitely many recurring schedules with finitely many isolated exceptions. A counterexample would reveal a return-time pattern outside that arithmetic structure.
problems.family: Dynamical Mordell–Lang Conjecture
problems.atlasNote: The2026primary introductions distinguish the full conjecture from etale, specified affine-plane and split-curve theorems. XYZ's product corollary has additional factor hypotheses and only DML(1) scope. A search-summary assertion of full resolution is not source evidence. Bounded review does not attest the absence of all other claims. consequences.positiveBranch: Every admissible return set would decompose into finitely many progressions, including singleton exceptions. The survey's periodic-subvariety consequence requires a wandering orbit and infinitely many distinct intersection points, and uses f^m(Z) contained in Z. The assertion alone does not provide an effective decomposition, a Skolem algorithm or a converse from mere periodic-subvariety existence.
consequences.negativeBranch: One rigorously established admissible return set lacking every such finite decomposition refutes the universal assertion. Positive-characteristic phenomena or partially defined rational maps do not suffice. Existing etale and specified other theorems remain valid; no failure of all arithmetic dynamical structure follows.

problems.title: Reliability Function of the Binary Symmetric Channel Below the Critical Rate
problems.statement: Determine the optimal fixed-blocklength reliability function of the memoryless binary symmetric channel without feedback for every crossover probability 0<p<1/2 and every rate 0<R<R_crit(p). With equiprobable messages, let P_e^*(n,R,p) be the minimum average block error under maximum-likelihood decoding among binary length-n codes of cardinality at least ceil(2^(nR)). Define E(R,p)=limsup_{n->infinity}[-log_2 P_e^*(n,R,p)]/n. Here H_2 is binary entropy and R_crit(p)=1-H_2(sqrt(p)/(sqrt(p)+sqrt(1-p))). Success requires matching achievable and converse exponents, or an equivalent evaluable exact characterization, for all these parameters. Restating the operational optimization or merely improving unmatched bounds is not a resolution.
problems.question: When each transmitted bit independently flips with probability 0<p<1/2 and there is no feedback, what is the best asymptotic exponent of average block-error decay? Determine it for fixed-blocklength codes at every positive rate below the channel's critical rate, optimizing over all codes with equally likely messages. Use the limsup of −log₂(error)/block length.
problems.why: An exact answer would identify the optimal tradeoff between information rate and error decay in this basic noisy channel. It would provide a performance benchmark; an efficient encoding or decoding algorithm would be a separate achievement.
problems.family: Channel reliability

problems.title: Equivalence or Strict Containment of QMA and QMA(2)
problems.statement: Determine whether QMA(2)=QMA in the ordinary unrelativized, uniform polynomial-time quantum verification model. For a promise problem (Y,N), QMA(2) allows two polynomial-size quantum witnesses, required to be a product across the two prover registers: each YES input has some such witness accepted with probability at least 2/3, and each NO input is accepted with probability at most 1/3 for every such witness. QMA allows one unrestricted polynomial-size quantum witness with the same bounds. There is no requirement outside the promise. The verifier uses a fixed standard universal quantum computation model, with no oracle or advice. The two complete outcomes are equality and strict containment QMA properly contained in QMA(2).
problems.question: Can two quantum proofs guaranteed to be unentangled certify more problems than one unrestricted quantum proof? In both cases the verifier must run in uniform polynomial time with bounded error, and the total proof length is polynomial in the input size.
problems.why: Equality would show that the two-witness product-state promise adds no verification power. Strict containment would demonstrate that enforcing separation between the witnesses enables verification of additional promise problems.

problems.title: Michel Boundary Rigidity Conjecture for Simple Manifolds
problems.statement: Let M be a compact smooth manifold with nonempty boundary of dimension n>=3, and g,g' smooth simple Riemannian metrics: the boundary is strictly convex, every two points are joined by a unique geodesic, and there are no conjugate points. Assert that whenever d_g(x,y)=d_g'(x,y) for all boundary points x,y, there exists a diffeomorphism phi:M->M equal to the identity pointwise on the boundary with g'=phi^*g.
problems.question: Can distances through a manifold between boundary points determine its interior geometry, up to a smooth coordinate change fixing the boundary? The question concerns compact manifolds of dimension at least three with nonempty strictly convex boundary, unique geodesics between points and no conjugate points.
problems.why: A proof would establish that these distance measurements determine the interior geometry within the stated simple-metric class. A counterexample would give indistinguishable boundary distances for interiors not related by an allowed change of coordinates.
problems.family: Michel Boundary Rigidity Conjecture for Simple Manifolds

consequences.negativeBranch: Prove existence of an in-scope simple metric pair with identical boundary distances and no boundary-pointwise-fixing diffeomorphism relating the metrics; no explicit counterexample or reconstruction algorithm is required.

problems.title: Alperin–McKay Conjecture
problems.statement: For every finite group G, every prime p, every p-block B of G with defect group D, and its Brauer correspondent b in N_G(D), the numbers k_0(B) and k_0(b) of ordinary irreducible complex characters of height zero are equal. For a character chi in a p-block of a finite group H with defect group D, height zero means chi(1)_p=|H:D|_p, where a_p is the largest power of p dividing the positive integer a.
problems.question: In a finite group's representation theory, does each p-block have exactly as many height-zero irreducible characters as its Brauer-correspondent block in the normalizer of a defect group? This predicts that a count of representations of the whole group is determined by this local subgroup.
problems.why: A proof would recover each global block's height-zero character count from its specified local normalizer block. It would establish equality of counts without requiring a canonical correspondence between individual characters.
problems.family: Alperin–McKay Conjecture
problems.atlasNote: Ruhstorfer's prime2 case is published in Annals201(2025),379–457, as independently checked on the journal page. MNST's Brauer-height-zero result and Cabanes–Spath's ordinary McKay result are distinct assertions. The read all-block, all-prime formulation remains open; root's bounded current search did not verify a universal AM resolution and does not certify absence of claims. The displayed status is retained from the selected, previously reviewed input, with its bound qualifications; no fresh current-status certification is claimed here.

consequences.positiveBranch: A proof establishes the prescribed equality between height-zero characters of each global block and its local normalizer block for all finite groups and primes. It supplies the exact blockwise local-global count, not a canonical bijection by itself.
consequences.negativeBranch: A disproof identifies failure of that blockwise local-global count. It does not refute the already-established ordinary McKay or Brauer-height-zero theorems, nor every stronger refinement without an explicit implication review.

problems.title: Planar homogeneous Mumford–Shah local-structure conjecture
problems.statement: Let Omega be any open subset of R^2. Consider every reduced absolute local minimizer (u,K) of E0(u,K;U)=integral_{U minus K}|grad u|^2 dx+H^1(K intersect U): K is relatively closed and countably 1-rectifiable, u is real and in W^{1,2}_loc(Omega minus K), E0 is finite on each relatively compact open U, and H^1(K intersect V)=0 implies K intersect V is empty for every open V contained in Omega. Absolute local minimality means E0(u,K;U)<=E0(v,J;U) for every relatively compact open U and every admissible locally finite-energy pair (v,J) for which (J symmetric-difference K) union the support of u-v is compactly contained in U; equality of functions off that compact set is understood almost everywhere on their common domain. There is no component-count or separation restriction on competitors. Must every x in K have a disk B_r(x) compactly contained in Omega and a C1 diffeomorphism Phi:B_r(x)->B_r(x), with Phi(x)=x and D Phi(x)=Id, such that Phi(K intersect B_r(x)) is one of: a diameter through x, one radius ending at x, or three radii ending at x with mutual120-degree angles?
problems.question: The planar homogeneous Mumford–Shah model balances changes in a field against the length of its crack set. For a reduced absolute local energy minimizer, must every interior crack point look, after a C¹ coordinate change, like a line, a single tip, or three branches meeting at 120°?
problems.why: A proof would classify the local structure at every interior point of the jump set into the three specified models. A counterexample would reveal another local geometry under the same unrestricted competitor rule.
problems.family: Planar homogeneous Mumford–Shah local-structure conjecture
problems.atlasNote: OpenAI release update, 6 October 2026: the full ranked target remains unclosed by these results. Exact scope reviewed; proofs not independently audited, refereeing not independently confirmed, and Lean artifacts not executed. Family 366: The supplied paper defines F_g=E0+integral |u-g|^2 with coefficient exactly one, on bounded Lipschitz domains, with bounded g, finite total crack length and u in L2 intersect W1,2 away from K. Its absolute competitors have the same compact-support comparison rule as the target and no component/separation restriction; its reducedness condition is also the target condition. Theorem 1.1 supplies C1,alpha interior arcs, crack tips and physical 120-degree triple junctions. The zero-fidelity case is not a stated parameter choice. There is a direct partial implication: a locally bounded homogeneous absolute minimizer can be restricted to a compactly contained disk and used with bounded fidelity datum g=u; its own fidelity term is zero and every competitor adds a nonnegative term, so it is an F_g absolute minimizer and inherits the local geometry. C1,alpha geometry implies the requested C1 straightening with derivative identity after choosing the model rays along the tangents. However the frozen homogeneous class assumes only local finite energy and does not impose local boundedness or L2 across K; the supplied boundedness proposition itself assumes F_g minimality with bounded g. It cannot be used circularly to obtain boundedness for an arbitrary E0 minimizer. Thus the locally bounded homogeneous subclass is covered, while a statement extending to all frozen admissible minimizers remains missing. Earlier qualification retained: Francesco Deangelis, arXiv:2609.26732v2 (5 October 2026; first version 22 September), claims the full planar Mumford-Shah interior regularity theorem. Theorem 1.1 includes reduced absolute local minimizers, lambda=0, and unrestricted competitor topology; the claimed arc, crack-tip and 120-degree triple-junction classification matches the fixed homogeneous target. Retain this entity at its inherited importance rank with a prominent pending-proof hold. No independent full proof audit, journal acceptance or public formalization was established in this review.

consequences.positiveBranch: A proof would establish the complete selected interior local structure of every homogeneous absolute minimizer, including crack-tip regularity and physical triple angles. It would resolve this variational regularity target; no efficient segmentation algorithm or theorem for all fidelity energies is automatically asserted.
consequences.negativeBranch: A disproof would establish an admissible reduced, locally finite-energy absolute homogeneous minimizer and an interior point where none of the three normalized local models applies. A failure for a restricted competitor class, nonzero fidelity parameter or domain-boundary point alone does not settle this target.

problems.title: Complex linearity of closed-surface mapping class groups by genus
problems.statement: For every integer g >= 3, let S_g be the closed connected orientable surface of genus g and Mod(S_g) its group of isotopy classes of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms. Determine exactly the set of such genera g for which there exist an integer n >= 1 and an injective homomorphism Mod(S_g) -> GL_n(C), with n allowed to depend on g. A complete resolution proves the answer for every g >= 3; one nonlinear genus, a bounded-dimensional obstruction, or an isolated family of representations without the remaining genus answers is partial progress.
problems.question: For exactly which genera g≥3 can the orientation-preserving symmetries of a closed orientable surface, identified up to continuous deformation, be represented faithfully by finite-dimensional complex matrices? The matrix dimension may depend on g, the number of handles.
problems.why: A complete answer would identify every genus whose mapping classes admit a faithful finite matrix description. It would distinguish those cases from genera where every such representation loses group information.

problems.title: Zagier Conjecture on Dedekind Zeta Values
problems.statement: For every number field F of signature (r1,r2) and every integer k>=2, put n=r2 for even k and n=r1+r2 for odd k. There exist xi_1,...,xi_n in A_k(F) tensor Q, using the allowable-symbol group defined by Zagier--Gangl section2, such that zeta_F(k) belongs to Q^times times sqrt(abs(D_F)) pi^{k([F:Q]-n)} det(L_k(sigma_i(xi_j)))_{1<=i,j<=n}. Here L_k is the single-valued polylogarithm defined there by the Bernoulli-number combination of classical polylogarithms (imaginary part for even k, real part for odd k), extended Q-linearly to symbols. For even k take one embedding from each conjugate complex pair; for odd k also take all real embeddings. The empty determinant is1. This is existence of the determinant formula, not the stronger regulator-lattice or Bloch-group rank assertion.
problems.question: Polylogarithms are higher relatives of the logarithm. Can every number field's Dedekind zeta value at an integer at least two be expressed using a determinant of single-valued polylogarithms, multiplied by a nonzero rational number and the predicted factors involving π and the field's discriminant?
problems.why: A proof would express these zeta values through a finite determinant of polylogarithmic data over the same field. It would establish the stated formula without requiring the stronger regulator-lattice assertions.
problems.family: Zagier Conjecture on Dedekind Zeta Values

consequences.negativeBranch: Prove existence of a number field F and integer k>=2 for which no specified allowable determinant formula exists; no explicit counterexample construction is required.

problems.title: Polynomial-time explicit logarithmic Ramsey graphs
problems.statement: Does there exist one deterministic algorithm A and constants C,c>0 such that, for every integer N>=2 given in unary, A outputs the adjacency matrix of a simple N-vertex graph in time at most O(N^c), with both its clique number and independence number at most C log_2 N? This is ordinary output-size polynomial explicitness, not poly(log N)-time adjacency queries.
problems.question: Can one deterministic algorithm construct an N-vertex graph in time polynomial in N with no set larger than a fixed constant times log N whose vertices are either all pairwise joined or all pairwise unjoined?
problems.why: A positive answer would make graphs with this logarithmic avoidance guarantee uniformly constructible in time polynomial in their size. It would produce the entire adjacency matrix, without requiring faster individual adjacency queries.
problems.family: Polynomial-time explicit logarithmic Ramsey graphs
problems.atlasNote: The ordinary explicit logarithmic target remains open in the bounded primary-source and current-status review. Sudakov–Tomon state the explicit gap; Chattopadhyay–Zuckerman and Li give weaker polylogarithmic parameters through stronger adjacency-explicit constructions. Current searches located no general logarithmic solution; off-diagonal, rank-Ramsey and finite numerical constructions are different tasks. The displayed status is retained from the selected, previously reviewed input, with its bound qualifications; no fresh current-status certification is claimed here.

consequences.positiveBranch: A proof would make the probabilistic logarithmic clique/independence order attainable by ordinary uniform polynomial-time graph production. It would close this explicit-versus-existence gap without necessarily giving an optimal extractor or strongly explicit adjacency oracle.
consequences.negativeBranch: A disproof would separate efficient uniform graph production from the known nonconstructive logarithmic Ramsey existence theorem. It must rule out all polynomial-time constructions, not merely algebraic or extractor-based approaches.

problems.title: Margulis–Zimmer Commensurated-Subgroup Conjecture over Number Fields
problems.statement: For every number field K, connected absolutely almost simple simply connected algebraic K-group G, finite set S of places containing all archimedean places, and subgroup Gamma of G(K) commensurable with G(O_S), suppose the sum over v in S of rank over K_v of G is at least two. For every subgroup N of Gamma such that N intersect gamma N gamma^(-1) has finite index in both N and gamma N gamma^(-1) for all gamma in Gamma, assert that N is finite or is commensurable with G(O_Sprime) for some set Sprime with all archimedean places contained in Sprime contained in S. Here O_S is the ring of S-integers and commensurability is inside G(K). Prove this universal assertion or give a counterexample. The target includes anisotropic/cocompact arithmetic lattices and mixed archimedean/nonarchimedean higher S-rank; it is not restricted to the non-uniform real-lattice cases.
problems.question: In an S-arithmetic group over a number field with total local rank at least two, must every commensurated subgroup be finite or commensurable with the arithmetic group obtained from a subset of the allowed places, possibly the full set? The question includes cocompact and mixed-place cases.
problems.why: This would classify subgroups that differ from each conjugate by only finite index. It asks for that classification across the full stated higher-rank arithmetic setting, including cases beyond non-uniform real lattices.
problems.family: Margulis–Zimmer Commensurated-Subgroup Conjecture over Number Fields
problems.atlasNote: The general number-field assertion remains open on the reviewed evidence; the July 2026 paper claims non-uniform cases under additional rank hypotheses.

consequences.positiveBranch: The subgroup classification would extend the stated arithmetic rigidity to commensurated subgroups across the full quantified number-field setting.
consequences.negativeBranch: An admissible infinite commensurated subgroup outside the listed arithmetic types would refute that classification, without refuting the normal-subgroup theorem.

problems.title: Grigorchuk Gap Conjecture
problems.statement: For every finitely generated group G with finite generating set X, let gamma_G,X(n) count elements of word length at most n in X union X^(-1). For positive functions on positive integers, write f preceq g if some integer C>=1 satisfies f(n)<=C g(Cn) for every n>=1, and f prec g if f preceq g but not g preceq f. Prove that gamma_G,X prec exp(sqrt(n)) implies that G has polynomial growth, equivalently that G is virtually nilpotent. The growth comparison is independent of the finite generating set. It is strict comparison of growth classes, not merely an eventual numerical upper bound or non-strict domination.
problems.question: Count the elements of a finitely generated group reachable in at most n generator steps. If this growth is strictly below exp(√n), when growth rates are compared up to constant rescaling of n and value, must it actually be bounded by a polynomial?
problems.why: A proof would exclude intermediate growth throughout this strict region and force such groups to be virtually nilpotent. A counterexample would place nonpolynomial growth below the proposed boundary.
problems.family: Grigorchuk Gap Conjecture
problems.atlasNote: The selected primary papers state the general one-half conjecture, and the November 2025 preprint reports only smaller-exponent progress within a restricted class. The bounded September 7 search found no accepted proof or counterexample for the exact all-finitely-generated-groups statement. The displayed status is retained from the selected, previously reviewed input, with its bound qualifications; no fresh current-status certification is claimed here.

consequences.positiveBranch: A positive resolution rules out non-polynomial group growth strictly below the proposed boundary class and extends the structural force of polynomial-growth theory to that whole strict region.
consequences.negativeBranch: A negative resolution supplies an intermediate-growth group below the proposed boundary and overturns the asserted universal gap, without automatically classifying the full spectrum of growth rates.

problems.title: Vassiliev Separation by Abelian-Valued Finite-Type Invariants
problems.statement: For every pair of non-isotopic smooth closed oriented unframed knots K_1,K_2 in S^3, assert that there exist an abelian group A, a nonnegative integer d and an A-valued Vassiliev invariant v of order at most d with v(K_1) != v(K_2). Knots are taken up to ambient isotopy respecting their orientation, so a knot and its reverse are included when they are distinct oriented knot types. Extend v linearly from the free abelian group on oriented knot types to singular knots by the usual alternating positive/negative crossing-resolution relation; order at most d means vanishing on every singular knot with d+1 transverse double points. The coefficient group and finite order may depend on the pair. Rational-valued, integer-valued and Kontsevich-injectivity variants are related but are not asserted equivalent here.
problems.question: Can finite-type knot invariants distinguish every pair of different oriented knot types in the three-sphere? These invariants have finite order under the crossing-change relation, and may take values in any abelian group, with both the order and group chosen for the pair.
problems.why: A proof would make the full permitted finite-type invariant system detect oriented knot type. A counterexample would exhibit distinct oriented knots indistinguishable by every finite order and every allowed coefficient group.
problems.family: Vassiliev Separation by Abelian-Valued Finite-Type Invariants

consequences.negativeBranch: An all-orders counterexample exposes a genuine limit of finite-type knot information even with arbitrary abelian coefficients, identifying oriented topology that this entire system cannot recover.

problems.statement: For every smooth projective complex Fano manifold F, prove the original Dubrovin conjecture in the form recalled in Galkin-Golyshev-Iritani Section 4.6: (1) the (big) quantum cohomology of F is generically semisimple if and only if the bounded derived category D^b_coh(F) admits a full exceptional collection; and, if the quantum cohomology is semisimple (quantum product convergent and semisimple at some point tau, with the monodromy data taken at tau and an admissible phase in that paper's conventions of Sections 2 and 4.5), there exists a full exceptional collection E_1,...,E_N such that (2) the Stokes matrix satisfies S_ij = chi(E_i,E_j) for all i,j, and (3) the central connection matrix factors as C = C'C'' where the columns of C'' are the components of the modified Chern characters Ch(E_j) and C' is an operator on cohomology commuting with cup product by c_1(F). Dubrovin predicts that generic semisimplicity of quantum cohomology occurs exactly when the derived category of sheaves has a full exceptional collection, with compatible numerical data where the quantum product converges and is semisimple.

problems.title: Chowla Non-Vanishing Conjecture for Dirichlet L-Functions at the Central Point
problems.statement: For every integer q>=1 and every primitive Dirichlet character chi of conductor q, including real and nonreal characters and both even and odd parity, the analytically continued Dirichlet L-function satisfies L(1/2,chi) != 0. The conductor-one character is included with L(s,chi)=zeta(s), whose central value is already known to be nonzero; conductors with no primitive characters contribute no cases. No positivity, quantitative lower bound, effective constant or off-central zero-free region is part of the assertion.

problems.statement: For every n≥1 and nonconstant f∈Q[x_1,...,x_n], there is a finite set S_f of primes such that for every p outside S_f, every complex-valued locally constant compactly supported function phi on Q_p^n, and every actual pole s_0 of the meromorphic continuation of Z_p(f,phi;s)=integral |f(x)|_p^s phi(x) dx, exp(2*pi*i*Re(s_0)) is an eigenvalue of the local complex monodromy of f at some point of {f=0}⊂C^n. Haar measure is normalized by vol(Z_p^n)=1; the nonzero normalization does not affect poles. This is the standard assertion of Veys Conjecture 2.12(1); S_f depends on f, not on phi. problems.title: Ivrii conjecture on periodic billiard orbits
problems.statement: For every integer n>=2 and every bounded connected open domain Ω in Euclidean R^n with C∞ boundary, prove the following assertion; neither convexity nor simple connectivity is assumed. Let M_reg be the set on which every forward and backward iterate is well-defined and nongrazing. For P=union over integers k>=2 of {z in M_reg: β^k(z)=z}, prove μ(P)=0. problems.title: Brauer-Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle for K3 surfaces
problems.statement: For every number field k and every K3 surface X over k (smooth projective geometrically integral surface with trivial canonical bundle and H^1(X, O_X) = 0), prove that X(A_k)^{Br(X)} nonempty implies X(k) nonempty. Here Br(X) = H^2_et(X, G_m), and X(A_k)^{Br(X)} is the set of adelic points (x_v) such that for every alpha in Br(X) the sum over all places v of inv_v(alpha(x_v)) vanishes in Q/Z, i.e. simultaneous orthogonality of one adelic point to the entire Brauer group. No assertion about weak approximation, about density of X(k) in X(A_k)^{Br(X)}, or about the existence of a single obstructing class is included.
problems.question: For a K3 surface over a number field, suppose there is one choice of points over all completions that passes every Brauer–Manin test at once. Must the surface then have a point over the number field itself?
problems.why: A proof would make the full Brauer–Manin obstruction sufficient for rational-point existence in this class. Failure would exhibit compatible local data passing every such condition while no rational point exists.

problems.title: NP-Hardness of Constant-Factor Approximation for Densest k-Subgraph
problems.statement: Let OPT(G,k)=max_{S subseteq V(G), |S|=k}|E(G[S])| for a finite simple undirected input graph G. Prove or refute the assertion that there exists an absolute constant epsilon>0 for which the promise problem of distinguishing OPT(G,k)>=t from OPT(G,k)<t/(1+epsilon), with input integers 1<=k<=|V(G)| and t>=1, is NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time gap reductions. The target is any fixed nontrivial constant approximation gap for exactly k vertices, based on NP-hardness rather than a stronger average-case or exponential-time assumption.
problems.question: In a given graph, choose exactly k vertices to capture as many edges as possible. Is there a fixed approximation factor greater than one for which this task is NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time reductions?
problems.why: A proof would establish constant-gap hardness for selecting exactly k vertices, with no stronger complexity assumption in the reduction. It would rule out polynomial-time solutions to this promise problem unless P equals NP.
problems.family: NP-Hardness of Constant-Factor Approximation for Densest k-Subgraph

problems.title: Pugh–Shub Stable Ergodicity (C^r Density in Partial Hyperbolicity)
problems.statement: For every compact connected boundaryless smooth manifold M with a smooth probability volume m, and every r in [2,infinity] (including the C^infinity topology), is the following true? In the space PH_m^r(M) of volume-preserving C^r partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms, maps that are C^1-stably ergodic among C^2 volume-preserving diffeomorphisms are C^r-dense. Thus every f in PH_m^r(M) and every relative C^r neighborhood U of f contain g such that some C^1 neighborhood V of g has every C^2 volume-preserving h in V ergodic for m. Use the usual C^r topology, with the Holder convention for nonintegral finite r. Partial hyperbolicity means a continuous Df-invariant dominated splitting TM=E^u+E^c+E^s: E^u and E^s are nontrivial, E^c may be zero, and for some common integer N>=1 the unstable unit vectors expand by >2, stable unit vectors contract by <1/2, and earlier nonzero bundles dominate later ones by a factor >2 under Df^N, pointwise at the same base point in that order. This is the ACW stability convention with the r>=2 range documented by RHRHU, not density among all conservative diffeomorphisms or only C^1-density.
problems.question: On a compact connected manifold without boundary, can every volume-preserving partially hyperbolic map be approximated in every Cʳ topology, r≥2 including ∞, by one that remains ergodic under small C¹ perturbations through C² volume-preserving maps? Ergodic means there is no invariant region of intermediate volume.
problems.why: A proof would guarantee robust ergodic behavior arbitrarily close in each stated smooth topology. A disproof would identify a regularity and a neighborhood within the partially hyperbolic class where that approximation fails.

problems.title: Conforti–Cornuéjols Conjecture: Packing Property Implies Max-Flow Min-Cut
problems.statement: For every finite clutter H, prove or disprove that its packing property implies its max-flow min-cut property. Use the following precise linear-programming convention, with M the edge-by-vertex0/1 incidence matrix: the packing property says that min{w^T x:Mx>=1,x>=0}=max{1^T y:M^T y<=w,y>=0} has integral optimal solutions on both sides for every w in {0,1,+infinity}^V for which the optimum is finite. An infinite cost forces that primal coordinate to0 and omits the corresponding dual upper-bound constraint. The MFMC property requires integral optimal solutions on both sides for every finite nonnegative integral w. Equivalently, packing means the covering/edge-packing min-max equality holds for all minors with the usual feasible-case convention. The reverse implication MFMC implies packing is already known.
problems.question: Does every finite clutter with the packing property also have the max-flow min-cut property? Both properties use the stated finite-optimum convention, so an infeasible covering program or an unbounded dual is not a counterexample.
problems.why: This would promote the packing condition to integral primal and dual optima for every finite nonnegative integral weight vector in the feasible, finite-optimum cases. The reverse implication is already known.

problems.title: Zilber's Exponential-Algebraic Closedness Conjecture
problems.statement: For every positive integer n and irreducible complex algebraic subvariety V of C^n x (C*)^n which is free and rotund, decide whether V contains (z,exp(z)) for some z in C^n. Free means that neither projection is contained in a translate of a proper Q-defined linear subspace or a proper algebraic subtorus, respectively. Rotund means dim(pi_L(V)) >= n-dim(L) for every Q-defined complex linear subspace L of C^n, where pi_L is the quotient to C^n/L x (C*)^n/exp(L). This is ordinary exponential-algebraic closedness, without an extra generic-transcendence-degree requirement.
problems.question: Treat complex variables and their exponentials as independent coordinates, producing an algebraic variety. If it is irreducible, free and rotund—conditions on rational linear and multiplicative constraints and on dimensions after quotients—must it contain a genuine point (z, exp(z))?
problems.why: The result would decide whether these algebraic freedom and dimension conditions force a solution to the corresponding polynomial-exponential equations. The target asks for existence without an additional generic-transcendence-degree requirement.

problems.title: Boundedness of Compact Hyperkahler Manifolds: Finiteness of Deformation Types in Each Dimension
problems.statement: For each integer n>=1, are there only finitely many deformation-equivalence classes of compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic complex manifolds of complex dimension 2n? Such a manifold is smooth, simply connected and compact Kähler, with H^0(X,Omega_X^2) spanned by a holomorphic two-form nondegenerate everywhere. Deformation equivalence is the equivalence generated by occurrence as fibers in smooth proper holomorphic families of such manifolds over connected bases. No projectivity, polarization, lattice, second-Betti-number or fibration restriction is imposed. Resolve by proving finiteness in every fixed dimension or showing infinitely many deformation classes in one fixed dimension.
problems.question: In each fixed even complex dimension, are there only finitely many deformation types of compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds? Deformations may pass through connected smooth proper holomorphic families; no projectivity, polarization or fibration assumption is imposed.
problems.why: Finiteness would place a basic limit on the variety of these manifolds in any one dimension. It would establish that only finitely many deformation classes occur, without requiring an explicit classification of all of them.

problems.title: Hilbert's Tenth Problem over C(t) with named t
problems.statement: Let t be a fixed transcendental indeterminate and C(t) the field of complex rational functions. Determine whether there exists an algorithm (Turing machine) which, given any n >= 1 and any polynomial f in Z[t][x_1,...,x_n], presented by its finite list of integer coefficients and monomial exponents in t and the x_i, halts and correctly decides whether f = 0 has a solution (x_1,...,x_n) in C(t)^n. Equivalently, determine whether the existential (positive existential) theory of the structure (C(t); 0, 1, +, -, *, t), with a constant symbol naming t and no constants for other complex numbers, is decidable. Inputs with arbitrary complex coefficients, and the ring language without a symbol for t, are not part of this target.
problems.question: Can an algorithm always decide whether a polynomial equation has solutions that are complex rational functions of one formal variable t? The input coefficients are integer-coefficient polynomials in that same named t, and any finite number of unknowns is allowed.
problems.why: The answer would locate the decision boundary for these finitely encoded equations with the indeterminate t named. An algorithm must halt on every input; undecidability would rule out such a universal procedure for this exact coefficient language.

problems.question: A P-matrix guarantees a unique solution to a linear complementarity problem, which combines linear equations, nonnegativity, and conditions preventing paired quantities from both being positive. Can that solution always be found in polynomial time for rational inputs?
problems.why: A positive answer would turn guaranteed uniqueness into an efficient exact solution method for this full input class. A negative answer would show that uniqueness does not ensure polynomial-time solvability here.

problems.title: Rationality Implies C2-Cofiniteness for Vertex Operator Algebras
problems.statement: For every complex vertex operator algebra V of CFT type, V=direct_sum_(n>=0) V_n with finite-dimensional graded pieces and V_0=C1, assume rationality in the sense that every admissible (N-gradable weak) V-module is a direct sum of simple admissible modules. Must dim_C(V/C2(V)) be finite, where C2(V)=span_C{u_(-2)v:u,v in V}? Prove the implication for all such V, or construct a rational CFT-type VOA with infinite-dimensional C2 quotient. No self-contragredient, unitarity or pre-existing C2-cofiniteness hypothesis is imposed. Semisimplicity restricted to ordinary modules alone is not the rationality hypothesis.
problems.question: Must a complex vertex operator algebra of CFT type have finite-dimensional V/C2(V) whenever every admissible module is a direct sum of simple admissible modules? No unitarity or self-contragredience assumption is added.
problems.why: This asks whether the stated representation-theoretic rationality forces the separate finiteness condition C2-cofiniteness. Semisimplicity of ordinary modules alone is a weaker hypothesis and is not the question here.

problems.title: Balanced L4 boundedness of the trilinear Hilbert transform
problems.statement: For Schwartz functions f,g,h:R->C, let T(f,g,h)(x)=p.v. integral_R f(x+t)g(x+2t)h(x+3t) dt/t. Is there a finite constant C such that ||T(f,g,h)||_{L^(4/3)(R)} <= C ||f||_{L^4(R)}||g||_{L^4(R)}||h||_{L^4(R)} for every such triple?
problems.question: The trilinear Hilbert transform combines three functions sampled at x+t, x+2t, and x+3t through a singular integral. Is its output's L⁴ᐟ³ norm always bounded by one constant times the product of the three L⁴ input norms, for smooth rapidly decaying inputs?
problems.why: A proof would control this singular integral uniformly over all triples, for its fixed shifts x+t, x+2t, and x+3t. Refutation would give triples whose normalized output size exceeds every constant.
problems.family: Balanced L4 boundedness of the trilinear Hilbert transform

problems.title: Matroid Secretary Conjecture
problems.statement: Determine whether there exist an absolute constant c>0 and an online algorithm A such that, for every finite known matroid M=(E,I) and every adversarially fixed nonnegative weight function w, A receives the elements in uniformly random order, learns an element's weight only when it arrives, makes irrevocable acceptance decisions, always maintains an independent accepted set ALG, and satisfies E[w(ALG)] >= c max_{S in I} w(S). The expectation is over the arrival order and any internal randomness of A; A may use the known matroid but not unseen weights.
problems.question: Items arrive in random order, revealing their nonnegative weights only as they arrive; each acceptance is final. Under any known matroid's rules for allowable sets, can one algorithm obtain, in expectation, a fixed positive fraction of the best total weight possible with full advance knowledge?
problems.why: A proof would guarantee a constant share of the best total weight despite decisions preceding knowledge of later weights. The constant must work uniformly across all finite known matroids and all permitted weight assignments.

problems.title: Piltz Divisor Problem for k-Fold Divisor Error Terms
problems.statement: For each integer k>=3, let d_k(n) count the ordered k-tuples of positive integers with product n, and let Delta_k(x)=sum_{n<=x} d_k(n)-Res_{s=1}(zeta(s)^k x^s/s). Determine alpha_k=inf{a: for every epsilon>0, Delta_k(x)=O_{k,epsilon}(x^(a+epsilon)) as x tends to infinity}.

problems.title: Erdős Matching Conjecture
problems.statement: For all positive integers k,s,n with n>=ks, let F be a family of distinct k-element subsets of [n]={1,...,n} containing no s pairwise disjoint members. The conjecture asserts |F|<=max{binom(ks-1,k), binom(n,k)-binom(n-s+1,k)}. Here binom(a,k)=0 for integers 0<=a<k. For s=1 the family is empty, and k=1 is included as a trivial case. The two terms are attained by all k-subsets of a fixed (ks-1)-set and by all k-subsets meeting a fixed (s-1)-set, respectively. Their role is sharpness of the bound, not an additional classification of all equality families.
problems.question: Choose k-element subsets of n objects, forbidding s mutually disjoint choices, with n≥ks. Is the maximum size always the larger of two constructions: all k-subsets inside ks−1 objects, or all k-subsets meeting a fixed set of s−1 objects?
problems.why: A negative answer would determine the exact largest size of every such family through the larger of the two constructions. A larger family would refute the formula without requiring a classification of all equality cases.

problems.title: Decidability of Finite Identity Bases for Finite Semigroups
problems.statement: Does a single algorithm exist which, on input the multiplication table of any finite semigroup S, halts and correctly decides whether all semigroup identities valid in S follow in equational logic from some finite set of identities? problems.statement: For every integer n>=3, let F_n be the free group on n generators. Equivalently, ask injectivity of the natural map from the profinite completion of Aut(F_n) to Aut of the profinite completion of F_n. problems.title: Residual Finiteness of All Artin-Tits Groups
problems.statement: Decide whether every Artin-Tits group associated with a finite Coxeter matrix is residually finite: for each nonidentity element g, there exists a homomorphism to a finite group whose value on g is nonidentity. No spherical, FC, triangle, or other diagram restriction is imposed.
problems.question: Is every Artin–Tits group defined by a finite Coxeter matrix residually finite: can each nonidentity element be distinguished from the identity in some finite quotient?
problems.why: This asks whether finite groups can detect every nontrivial element of these groups. A positive answer would establish this separation property for all such groups, beyond the classes where it is already known.
problems.family: Geometry and topology of Artin groups
problems.atlasNote: Current bounded literature search through 2023–2026 found partial results but no verified general resolution; this is not exhaustive certification.

consequences.positiveBranch: A positive resolution establishes the full assertion in the reviewed target and all of its stated special cases.
consequences.negativeBranch: Exhibit a finite-matrix Artin group A and a nonidentity element g such that every homomorphism from A to every finite group sends g to the identity.
